domain: Section 1: Setting up a cloud solution environment

questions.title: Org-wide control that covers future projects
questions.summary: IAM and org policy are inherited downward, so binding at the organisation node covers all current and future descendants.
questions.question: A new organisation policy must apply to every project your company owns, including projects that will be created next year in folders that don't exist yet. You want to set it once and never revisit it. Where should you set the policy?

options.A: On each existing project, and in the script that creates new projects.
options.B: On the organisation resource.
options.C: On the folder that holds the production projects.
options.D: On a tag that you bind to each project as it is created.

explanation.summary: Organisation policies set on the organisation resource are inherited by every folder and project under it, including ones created later, so one setting covers the whole estate.

option_breakdown.A: It works only while every future project goes through that script; a project created any other way is missed.
option_breakdown.B: Correct. A policy on the organisation resource is inherited by every folder and project beneath it, present and future.
option_breakdown.C: Projects in other folders, or directly under the organisation, don't inherit from that folder.
option_breakdown.D: A tag-conditioned policy still depends on someone binding the tag to each new project, which is the step to avoid.

explanation.gcloud_command:
gcloud org-policies set-policy policy.yaml
# policy.yaml names organizations/ORG_ID/policies/CONSTRAINT_NAME

questions.title: Departmental access boundary
questions.summary: A folder is the inheritance boundary for a department: bind once, and every current and future child project inherits.
questions.question: The finance department's projects — and only those — must share one set of access controls. Finance creates new projects each quarter and expects them to pick up the same controls automatically, without affecting other departments. What should you do?

options.A: Tag every finance resource with a label and write an IAM condition on the label in each project.
options.B: Grant the finance groups their roles at the organisation node.
options.C: Create a Finance folder, move the finance projects into it, and grant the roles on the folder.
options.D: Grant the roles on each finance project, and add them to every new finance project as it is created.

explanation.summary: A folder is the inheritance boundary for a department: one binding covers every current and future project in it and nothing outside it.

option_breakdown.A: Labels are not an IAM control — conditions use resource-manager tags or names, not labels — and per-project conditions still have to be repeated.
option_breakdown.B: An organisation grant reaches every department, which breaks the “only finance” boundary.
option_breakdown.C: Correct. A folder is the inheritance boundary for a department: one binding covers every current and future project in it and nothing outside it.
option_breakdown.D: Per-project grants do not reach projects created next quarter unless someone remembers to add them.

questions.title: Isolating regulated workloads
questions.summary: A dedicated folder gives regulated projects a single inheritance point and makes the compliance boundary explicit.
questions.question: Projects that hold regulated data must inherit a stricter set of IAM and organisation policies, and the compliance boundary must be visible in the resource hierarchy. New regulated projects are created every quarter. How should you structure this?

options.A: Label each regulated project regulated=true and target the policies at that label.
options.B: Put the regulated workloads in their own VPC network inside the existing projects.
options.C: Set the stricter policies on the organisation resource.
options.D: Create a Regulated folder, set the policies there, and create those projects in it.

explanation.summary: A folder is an inheritance point: policies set on it apply to every project inside it, now and later, and the folder makes the boundary visible in the hierarchy.

option_breakdown.A: Labels organise billing and filtering; IAM and organisation policies are not inherited through labels.
option_breakdown.B: A separate network isolates traffic, not IAM or policy, and the regulated data still shares projects with everything else.
option_breakdown.C: Every project in the company would inherit the stricter policies, not only the regulated ones.
option_breakdown.D: Correct. Every project created in the folder inherits its policies, and the folder itself shows the compliance boundary.

questions.title: Sandbox exception that must not leak
questions.summary: The project is the narrowest scope that still carries IAM and org policy, so an exception there cannot leak upward or sideways.
questions.question: The organisation denies external IP addresses on VMs through an organisation policy. One sandbox project needs that relaxed for experiments, and the exception must not reach any other project, now or in the future. Where should you set the exception?

options.A: On the sandbox project, overriding the inherited policy.
options.B: On the folder that contains the sandbox project.
options.C: On the organisation resource.
options.D: On each VM in the sandbox project.

explanation.summary: A policy set on a project can override the one it inherits, and it applies to that project only, so the exception cannot reach anything else.

option_breakdown.A: Correct. A project-level policy overrides the inherited one for that project and nothing else.
option_breakdown.B: Every other project in that folder, and any added to it later, would inherit the relaxed policy.
option_breakdown.C: Relaxing it on the organisation resource removes the protection everywhere.
option_breakdown.D: Organisation policies are set on the organisation, folders and projects; there is no policy on an individual VM.

explanation.gcloud_command:
gcloud org-policies set-policy sandbox-policy.yaml
# name: projects/SANDBOX_ID/policies/compute.vmExternalIpAccess, with an allow-all rule

questions.title: Organisation-wide asset visibility for auditors
questions.summary: Only an organisation-node binding gives visibility across all folders and projects, including ones created later.
questions.question: Auditors must be able to inventory every resource the company runs, wherever it sits in the hierarchy, without anyone having to remember to grant them access to newly created folders. What should you do?

options.A: Grant the auditors' group roles/cloudasset.viewer on every project today, and add it to each new project as it is created.
options.B: Grant the auditors' group roles/cloudasset.viewer on the largest folder, where most projects live.
options.C: Grant the auditors' group roles/cloudasset.viewer at the organisation node.
options.D: Export an Asset Inventory snapshot to a bucket each month and share the bucket with the auditors.

explanation.summary: A binding at the organisation inherits to every folder and project, including ones created later, and Cloud Asset Viewer lets the auditors search and export the whole inventory.

option_breakdown.A: Per-project grants must be repeated for every new project — exactly the step the requirement says nobody should have to remember.
option_breakdown.B: A folder grant leaves every project outside that folder invisible, so the inventory is incomplete.
option_breakdown.C: Correct. A binding at the organisation inherits to every folder and project, including ones created later, and Cloud Asset Viewer lets the auditors search and export the whole inventory.
option_breakdown.D: A monthly export is stale between runs and gives no live search; it also creates a copy to secure.

questions.title: Block public IPs except on a bastion
questions.summary: compute.vmExternalIpAccess is a list constraint: deny by default, allow-list the bastion.
questions.question: Engineers keep creating development VMs with external IP addresses. Security wants VM creation with an external IP to fail in every project except one bastion project. What should you do?

options.A: Create a firewall rule in each project that denies ingress from 0.0.0.0/0.
options.B: Enforce the constraint compute.skipDefaultNetworkCreation on the organisation.
options.C: Remove the default network from every project except the bastion project.
options.D: Enforce compute.vmExternalIpAccess on the organisation and override it in the bastion project.

explanation.summary: The compute.vmExternalIpAccess list constraint makes creating a VM with an external IP fail. Denied at the organisation and overridden on the bastion project, it blocks external IPs everywhere else.

option_breakdown.A: A firewall rule filters traffic; the VMs still get external IPs, and the rule must be repeated per project.
option_breakdown.B: It only stops new projects getting a default network; VMs on other networks can still have external IPs.
option_breakdown.C: Custom networks still allow external IPs, so removing the default network blocks nothing.
option_breakdown.D: Correct. The constraint rejects external IPs at creation time, and the project-level override exempts only the bastion project.

explanation.gcloud_command:
gcloud org-policies set-policy deny-external-ip.yaml
# name: organizations/ORG_ID/policies/compute.vmExternalIpAccess, rules: - denyAll: true

questions.title: Keep external identities out of IAM policies
questions.summary: iam.allowedPolicyMemberDomains rejects policy members outside the listed customer IDs at write time.
questions.question: An audit requires that IAM policies anywhere in the organisation never contain identities from outside the company's own Cloud Identity domain, and that attempts to add one are rejected rather than reported afterwards. What should you configure?

options.A: The constraint iam.allowedPolicyMemberDomains, set to the company's customer ID.
options.B: A log-based alert on SetIamPolicy entries that add external members.
options.C: A rule that only the security team holds Project IAM Admin.
options.D: Workforce Identity Federation for the company's identity provider.

explanation.summary: Domain restricted sharing (iam.allowedPolicyMemberDomains) limits IAM policy members to the listed customer IDs, so adding an external identity is rejected when the policy is written.

option_breakdown.A: Correct. The constraint rejects any IAM policy change that adds a member from outside the allowed customer IDs.
option_breakdown.B: An alert reports the change after it has happened; the requirement is to reject it.
option_breakdown.C: Fewer people can edit IAM, but those who can are still free to add external identities.
option_breakdown.D: Federation lets the company's own IdP users sign in; it does nothing to stop other domains being granted roles.

explanation.gcloud_command:
gcloud org-policies set-policy drs.yaml
# name: organizations/ORG_ID/policies/iam.allowedPolicyMemberDomains, allowedValues: [CUSTOMER_ID]

questions.title: Force teams off downloadable keys
questions.summary: iam.disableServiceAccountKeyCreation removes the ability to mint downloadable keys org-wide.
questions.question: To move every team onto keyless authentication, no one in the organisation may be able to create a downloadable service account key any more. Which control should you enforce?

options.A: The constraint iam.disableServiceAccountKeyUpload.
options.B: The constraint iam.disableServiceAccountKeyCreation.
options.C: The constraint iam.serviceAccountKeyExpiryHours, set to 24 hours.
options.D: Removal of the Service Account Key Admin role from every user.

explanation.summary: iam.disableServiceAccountKeyCreation is the boolean constraint that stops anyone creating service account keys, wherever it is enforced.

option_breakdown.A: This blocks uploading your own public keys; Google-generated keys can still be created and downloaded.
option_breakdown.B: Correct. Enforced on the organisation, it stops service account key creation in every project.
option_breakdown.C: Keys can still be created; they just expire after a day.
option_breakdown.D: Owner, Editor and other roles also include iam.serviceAccountKeys.create, and a new grant could restore it.

explanation.gcloud_command:
gcloud org-policies set-policy no-sa-keys.yaml
# name: organizations/ORG_ID/policies/iam.disableServiceAccountKeyCreation, rules: - enforce: true

questions.title: Enforce EU data residency
questions.summary: gcp.resourceLocations restricts the locations in which resources may be created.
questions.question: Data residency rules require that all new resources in the organisation are created only in European locations, enforced at creation rather than corrected later. What should you configure?

options.A: A default region of europe-west1 in every gcloud configuration.
options.B: VPC subnets in European regions only.
options.C: The constraint gcp.resourceLocations, allowing the in:eu-locations group.
options.D: A budget alert for spend on non-European SKUs.

explanation.summary: gcp.resourceLocations restricts where location-based resources can be created, so creation outside the allowed locations fails.

option_breakdown.A: A client default only fills in a missing flag; anyone can still pass another region.
option_breakdown.B: Subnets constrain VMs on that network, not buckets, datasets or other services.
option_breakdown.C: Correct. Creation in a location outside the allowed group is rejected.
option_breakdown.D: An alert reports spend after the resources exist; nothing is blocked.

explanation.gcloud_command:
gcloud org-policies set-policy locations.yaml
# name: organizations/ORG_ID/policies/gcp.resourceLocations, allowedValues: [in:eu-locations]

questions.title: Require Shielded VM on every instance
questions.summary: compute.requireShieldedVm makes instance creation fail unless Shielded VM protections are on.
questions.question: Every new Compute Engine VM in the organisation must boot with Secure Boot, vTPM and integrity monitoring, and VM creation must fail if it would not. What should you do?

options.A: Publish only Shielded VM-capable images in the company's image project.
options.B: Enforce the constraint compute.requireOsLogin on the organisation.
options.C: Enable Confidential VM in every instance template.
options.D: Enforce the constraint compute.requireShieldedVm on the organisation.

explanation.summary: compute.requireShieldedVm makes VM creation fail unless the VM uses a Shielded VM image with Secure Boot, vTPM and integrity monitoring enabled.

option_breakdown.A: Capable images allow Shielded VM, but a VM can still be created with the options turned off.
option_breakdown.B: OS Login controls SSH access, not how a VM boots.
option_breakdown.C: Confidential VM encrypts memory in use; it doesn't enforce Secure Boot, and templates don't stop other creation paths.
option_breakdown.D: Correct. The constraint rejects any new VM that would not boot with the Shielded VM protections.

explanation.gcloud_command:
gcloud org-policies set-policy shielded.yaml
# name: organizations/ORG_ID/policies/compute.requireShieldedVm, rules: - enforce: true

questions.title: Prevent public buckets organisation-wide
questions.summary: storage.publicAccessPrevention blocks allUsers and allAuthenticatedUsers grants for its whole scope.
questions.question: No Cloud Storage bucket in the organisation may ever be readable by allUsers or allAuthenticatedUsers, and project owners must not be able to opt out. What should you enforce?

options.A: The constraint storage.publicAccessPrevention on the organisation.
options.B: The constraint storage.uniformBucketLevelAccess on the organisation.
options.C: Public access prevention on each existing bucket.
options.D: An alert on audit log entries that add allUsers to a bucket.

explanation.summary: Enforcing storage.publicAccessPrevention on the organisation turns on public access prevention for every bucket under it, and project owners cannot turn it off.

option_breakdown.A: Correct. Inherited by every project, it blocks allUsers and allAuthenticatedUsers access to all buckets, current and new.
option_breakdown.B: Uniform access removes ACLs, but IAM can still grant allUsers.
option_breakdown.C: New buckets don't get it, and project owners can turn it off on their buckets.
option_breakdown.D: An alert reports a public bucket after it exists; nothing is prevented.

explanation.gcloud_command:
gcloud org-policies set-policy pap.yaml
# name: organizations/ORG_ID/policies/storage.publicAccessPrevention, rules: - enforce: true

questions.title: Link projects without seeing spend
questions.summary: Billing Account User is exactly the link-projects permission, with no read access to cost data.
questions.question: A team lead creates new projects and is their owner. They must also be able to link those projects to the central billing account, but company policy says they must not see the organisation's spend. Which role should you grant on the billing account, following least privilege?

options.A: Billing Account Administrator
options.B: Billing Account User
options.C: Billing Account Viewer
options.D: Billing Account Costs Manager

explanation.summary: Linking a project needs permission on the project (which an owner has) and on the billing account. Billing Account User gives the billing-account side without access to cost data.

option_breakdown.A: It can link projects, but it also shows all costs and manages the account, which policy forbids.
option_breakdown.B: Correct. It allows linking projects to the account and nothing that reveals spend.
option_breakdown.C: It shows exactly the spend the lead must not see, and it can't link projects.
option_breakdown.D: It manages budgets and views costs, which breaks the policy, and it isn't the linking permission.

questions.title: Read-only cost reporting
questions.summary: Billing Account Viewer is read-only across the billing account, its cost data and its budgets.
questions.question: At Harrowgate Mills, a finance analyst builds monthly reports from cost and budget data for every project on the company's single billing account. Audit requires that the analyst cannot change budgets, payment settings or project links. Which role should you grant?

options.A: Project Billing Manager on each project
options.B: Billing Account Costs Manager on the billing account
options.C: Billing Account Viewer on the billing account
options.D: Billing Account Administrator on the billing account

explanation.summary: Billing Account Viewer grants read-only access to the billing account, its cost data and its budgets, which is exactly a reporting role.

option_breakdown.A: It changes which billing account a project uses, and it shows no billing account costs.
option_breakdown.B: It reads costs but can also create and change budgets, which the analyst must not do.
option_breakdown.C: Correct. Billing Account Viewer gives read-only access to the account's cost data and budgets, which is a reporting role.
option_breakdown.D: It can change everything on the account, far beyond read-only.

questions.title: Move a project between billing accounts
questions.summary: Project Billing Manager is scoped to the project and controls only the project-to-billing-account association.
questions.question: Finance has granted a team lead Billing Account User on both of the company's billing accounts. The lead is not an owner of the project, but must be able to move it from one billing account to the other. Which role should you grant the lead on the project, following least privilege?

options.A: Owner
options.B: Billing Account Administrator
options.C: Editor
options.D: Project Billing Manager

explanation.summary: Changing a project's billing account needs permission on the billing account (Billing Account User) and on the project. Project Billing Manager is the project-side role that does only that.

option_breakdown.A: Owner includes the permission but also full control of every resource in the project.
option_breakdown.B: It is a billing-account role, not a project role, and it gives full control of the accounts.
option_breakdown.C: Editor does not include the permission to change a project's billing account.
option_breakdown.D: Correct. It lets the lead link and unlink the project's billing account and nothing else.

explanation.gcloud_command:
gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding PROJECT_ID \
  --member='user:lead@example.com' --role='roles/billing.projectManager'
gcloud billing projects link PROJECT_ID --billing-account=NEW_ACCOUNT_ID

questions.title: Subsidiary opens its own billing account
questions.summary: Billing Account Creator at the org node permits creating new billing accounts and nothing more.
questions.question: The finance team of a new subsidiary must be able to create the subsidiary's own billing account under the existing organisation, without being given any rights on the parent company's billing account. What should you grant them?

options.A: Billing Account Creator on the organisation.
options.B: Billing Account Administrator on the parent's billing account.
options.C: Project Creator on the organisation.
options.D: Billing Account User on the parent's billing account.

explanation.summary: Billing Account Creator, granted on the organisation, lets a principal create new billing accounts there; it grants nothing on existing accounts.

option_breakdown.A: Correct. It allows creating billing accounts in the organisation and nothing on the parent's account.
option_breakdown.B: This gives full control of the parent's account, which is what must be avoided, and it can't create a new account.
option_breakdown.C: It creates projects, not billing accounts.
option_breakdown.D: It links projects to the parent's account, which is a right on that account, and creates nothing.

questions.title: Full ownership of a billing account
questions.summary: Billing Account Administrator is the full-control role covering users, budgets and project linkage.
questions.question: One person must manage a billing account end to end: who has access to it, its budgets, and which projects are linked to it. Which single role on the billing account covers all of that?

options.A: Billing Account Costs Manager
options.B: Billing Account Administrator
options.C: Billing Account User
options.D: Billing Account Viewer

explanation.summary: Billing Account Administrator is the full-control role on a billing account: it manages access, budgets and linked projects.

option_breakdown.A: It manages budgets and cost data, but not who has access or which projects are linked.
option_breakdown.B: Correct. It covers access management, budgets and project links on the account.
option_breakdown.C: It can link projects to the account, but it can't manage access or budgets.
option_breakdown.D: It is read-only.

questions.title: Threshold alerts at 50/90/100 percent
questions.summary: A budget scoped to the project with multiple threshold rules emails the billing recipients.
questions.question: Finance wants an email when monthly spend on the analytics project reaches 50%, 90% and 100% of a fixed amount. No automated action is needed. What should you configure, with the least setup?

options.A: A cost anomaly alert on the billing account.
options.B: A billing export to BigQuery with a scheduled query that emails the totals.
options.C: A budget for the project with threshold rules at 50%, 90% and 100%.
options.D: A budget that publishes to Pub/Sub, with a Cloud Run function that sends email.

explanation.summary: A Cloud Billing budget scoped to the project, with threshold rules at each percentage, sends email notifications when actual or forecasted spend crosses them.

option_breakdown.A: Anomaly alerts fire on unusual deviations from history, not at fixed percentages of an amount.
option_breakdown.B: It works, but needs an export, a query and a mailer, and the export lags; a budget does this directly.
option_breakdown.C: Correct. Each threshold rule triggers an email when spend crosses it, with no code.
option_breakdown.D: Pub/Sub is for automated reactions; writing a function to send mail is more setup than a budget's built-in email.

questions.title: Automatically stop a sandbox over budget
questions.summary: Budget notifications on Pub/Sub can trigger a function that calls the Compute Engine API.
questions.question: When a sandbox project passes its monthly budget, the company wants its VMs stopped automatically rather than an email sent to someone who may be asleep. How should you set this up?

options.A: A budget with email notifications to the on-call engineer.
options.B: Lower the project's CPU quota to what the budget buys.
options.C: Cost anomaly detection with notifications for the project.
options.D: A budget that publishes to Pub/Sub, and a Cloud Run function that stops the VMs.

explanation.summary: Budgets only notify; they never stop spending. Publishing budget notifications to Pub/Sub lets a function react, for example by stopping the project's VMs.

option_breakdown.A: Email informs a person and takes no action, which is the gap described.
option_breakdown.B: Quotas limit how much can exist, not what it costs; it would also block legitimate use below the budget.
option_breakdown.C: Anomaly notifications report unusual spend; they take no action either.
option_breakdown.D: Correct. The function receives each budget notification and stops the VMs when spend exceeds the amount.

questions.title: Alert on forecast rather than actual spend
questions.summary: Budgets support a forecasted-spend threshold basis, firing on the projected total.
questions.question: A department wants a single warning when its *forecasted* month-end spend is on track to exceed its allocation, rather than waiting until the money is already spent. What should you configure?

options.A: Create a budget for the department's projects with a threshold rule on forecasted spend at 100%.
options.B: Create a budget with threshold rules on actual spend at 90% and 100%.
options.C: Lower the department's Compute Engine quotas to match its allocation.
options.D: Schedule a monthly query over the billing export that compares spend with the allocation.

explanation.summary: A threshold rule with the forecasted-spend basis fires when the projected month-end total crosses the amount — before the money is spent.

option_breakdown.A: Correct. A threshold rule with the forecasted-spend basis fires when the projected month-end total crosses the amount — before the money is spent.
option_breakdown.B: Actual-spend thresholds fire only once the money has been consumed, which is what the department wants to avoid.
option_breakdown.C: A quota caps capacity and would interrupt workloads; it does not warn anyone about cost.
option_breakdown.D: A monthly query reports after the month has ended — too late to act on a forecast.

questions.title: Chargeback model per business unit
questions.summary: Detailed billing export to BigQuery is the only source with per-SKU, per-resource rows carrying labels.
questions.question: From now on, the FinOps team needs per-SKU cost rows, with each resource's labels, in a form they can join with their own ownership table to build a chargeback model per business unit. What should you enable?

options.A: Cost table reports in the Cloud Billing console, grouped by label.
options.B: Detailed usage cost export from Cloud Billing to BigQuery.
options.C: A budget per business unit, filtered by label.
options.D: Cloud Asset Inventory export of every resource's labels to BigQuery.

explanation.summary: Detailed usage cost export writes per-SKU, per-resource cost rows with labels to a BigQuery dataset, where they can be joined with other tables.

option_breakdown.A: Console reports can group by label, but they can't be joined with another table.
option_breakdown.B: Correct. The export gives queryable cost rows with labels that can be joined with the ownership table.
option_breakdown.C: Budgets track spend against an amount; they don't produce cost rows.
option_breakdown.D: This exports resource metadata and labels, not what anything cost.

explanation.gcloud_command: # Console > Billing > Billing export > BigQuery export > Detailed usage cost > Edit settings

questions.title: Attribute costs inside one shared project
questions.summary: Labels applied to resources flow into billing data, enabling per-team grouping.
questions.question: Several teams run workloads in one shared project. Each team's costs must be attributable to it in the billing reports, without splitting the project. What should you do?

options.A: Give each team's VMs their own network tag.
options.B: Put each team's resources in its own subnet.
options.C: Apply a team label to each team's resources.
options.D: Run each team's workloads under its own service account.

explanation.summary: Labels on resources are carried into Cloud Billing data, so costs can be filtered and grouped by team inside one project.

option_breakdown.A: Network tags drive firewall rules and routes; they don't appear in billing data.
option_breakdown.B: Subnets separate addresses, not costs.
option_breakdown.C: Correct. Billing reports and the export can group costs by the team label.
option_breakdown.D: The identity a workload runs as isn't a cost attribute in billing reports.

questions.title: Active Directory as the source of truth
questions.summary: GCDS reads AD/LDAP on a schedule and creates, updates and suspends the matching Cloud Identity users and groups.
questions.question: Your organisation keeps its authoritative employee list in on-premises Active Directory and wants to keep it that way, while having full control over the Google accounts employees use for all Google services. The same users and groups must exist in Cloud Identity and stay updated as staff change. What should you do?

options.A: Run Google Cloud Directory Sync from Active Directory on a schedule.
options.B: Configure SAML single sign-on between Active Directory and Cloud Identity.
options.C: Create the accounts by hand in the Google Admin console.
options.D: Configure Workforce Identity Federation with Active Directory.

explanation.summary: Google Cloud Directory Sync reads Active Directory on a schedule and creates, updates and suspends the matching Cloud Identity users and groups, so the directory stays authoritative.

option_breakdown.A: Correct. GCDS keeps Cloud Identity users and groups in step with Active Directory, and the accounts are fully managed Google accounts.
option_breakdown.B: SSO changes how users sign in; it creates no users or groups, so Cloud Identity would not follow the directory.
option_breakdown.C: Hand-made accounts drift from Active Directory, and joiners and leavers depend on someone remembering.
option_breakdown.D: Federation avoids Google accounts altogether, so there would be no managed accounts for other Google services.

explanation.gcloud_command: ./sync-cmd -a -c config.xml   # scheduled; GCDS is configured with Configuration Manager

questions.title: No second password for Google Cloud
questions.summary: SAML SSO delegates authentication to the existing IdP, so no separate Google password exists.
questions.question: Every employee already has a Cloud Identity account, synchronised from the corporate directory, and signs in to everything else through the corporate identity provider. Management insists they must not have a separate password for Google Cloud. What should you configure?

options.A: Configure Workforce Identity Federation so users access Google Cloud with their existing identity provider credentials.
options.B: Configure SAML-based single sign-on between the external identity provider and Cloud Identity.
options.C: Use the transfer tool to bring existing unmanaged accounts under the organisation.
options.D: Use Google Cloud Directory Sync to provision users and groups from the on-premises directory.

explanation.summary: SAML SSO delegates authentication to the existing identity provider, so users sign in with their corporate credentials and no separate Google password exists.

option_breakdown.A: Workforce Identity Federation is for users who have no Cloud Identity account at all; these users already have accounts, so the need is to change how they sign in, not to add a second identity model.
option_breakdown.B: Correct. SAML SSO delegates authentication to the existing identity provider, so users sign in with their corporate credentials and no separate Google password exists.
option_breakdown.C: The transfer tool only addresses consumer accounts created with your domain before Cloud Identity existed; it is not a provisioning or authentication mechanism.
option_breakdown.D: Directory Sync provisions accounts, and they already exist; it does not change how users authenticate, so they would still have a Google password.

explanation.gcloud_command: # Admin console > Security > Authentication > SSO with third-party IdP

questions.title: Thousands of contractors without accounts
questions.summary: Workforce Identity Federation grants access to external workforce identities with no per-user account.
questions.question: Several thousand contractors from a partner organisation need short-lived access to Google Cloud. Provisioning and paying for a Cloud Identity account for each of them is unacceptable. What should you configure?

options.A: Sync the partner's directory into Cloud Identity with Google Cloud Directory Sync.
options.B: Set up SAML single sign-on from the partner's identity provider.
options.C: Set up Workforce Identity Federation with the partner's identity provider.
options.D: Share one service account key with the partner's administrators.

explanation.summary: Workforce Identity Federation grants Google Cloud access directly to external workforce identities through a workforce pool, with no per-user Cloud Identity account to create or pay for.

option_breakdown.A: Syncing creates a Cloud Identity account per contractor, which is exactly what is unacceptable.
option_breakdown.B: SSO signs users in to Cloud Identity accounts, so each contractor would still need one.
option_breakdown.C: Correct. Workforce Identity Federation grants Google Cloud access directly to external workforce identities through a workforce pool, with no per-user Cloud Identity account to create or pay for.
option_breakdown.D: A shared, long-lived key gives no per-person identity or audit trail and is easy to leak.

questions.title: Offboarding must revoke cloud access automatically
questions.summary: Directory Sync suspends accounts whose source records disappear, so AD offboarding propagates.
questions.question: When an employee leaves, their Google Cloud access must disappear as a consequence of the existing HR offboarding process, which updates Active Directory. No separate cloud step may be required. What should you do?

options.A: Ask HR to remove each leaver from every Google group by hand.
options.B: Create each new employee's Cloud Identity account by hand.
options.C: Turn on 2-step verification for every Cloud Identity account.
options.D: Run Google Cloud Directory Sync from Active Directory on a schedule.

explanation.summary: GCDS makes Active Directory the source of truth: when HR disables or removes the user there, the next sync suspends the Cloud Identity account, and every IAM grant stops working.

option_breakdown.A: A manual step is exactly what the requirement forbids, and it will eventually be missed.
option_breakdown.B: Manual creation keeps no link to Active Directory, so a leaver's account stays active.
option_breakdown.C: 2-step verification strengthens sign-in; it does nothing when someone leaves.
option_breakdown.D: Correct. GCDS makes Active Directory the source of truth: when HR disables or removes the user there, the next sync suspends the Cloud Identity account, and every IAM grant stops working.

explanation.gcloud_command: ./sync-cmd -a -c config.xml   # suspends users removed from the source LDAP

questions.title: Employees signed up with company email
questions.summary: The transfer tool brings unmanaged consumer accounts under organisational control.
questions.question: An audit finds that before Cloud Identity was adopted, employees created personal Google accounts using their company email addresses. These accounts sit outside the organisation and cannot be governed. What should you do?

options.A: Use the transfer tool for unmanaged users.
options.B: Create managed accounts for the same addresses with Directory Sync.
options.C: Set up SAML single sign-on for the domain.
options.D: Ask employees to delete their personal accounts.

explanation.summary: These are unmanaged accounts; the transfer tool for unmanaged users brings them under the organisation so they can be governed, audited and suspended like any other account.

option_breakdown.A: Correct. These are unmanaged accounts; the transfer tool invites their owners to move them under the organisation, where they can be governed, audited and suspended.
option_breakdown.B: Creating a managed account for an address that has an unmanaged account leaves the user with a conflicting account; the existing account and its data are not brought in.
option_breakdown.C: SSO applies to managed accounts; these accounts sit outside the organisation, so it doesn't reach them.
option_breakdown.D: Nothing enforces it, and the employees lose whatever the accounts hold.

explanation.gcloud_command: # Admin console > Account > Account settings > Transfer tool for unmanaged users

questions.title: API not enabled on a new project
questions.summary: New projects have most APIs disabled; enable the named service on the project.
questions.question: A deployment into a brand new project fails with 'API [compute.googleapis.com] not enabled on project'. What should you do?

options.A: Request a higher Compute Engine quota.
options.B: Enable the Compute Engine API on the project.
options.C: Grant the deploying account Compute Admin.
options.D: Retry the deployment with exponential backoff.

explanation.summary: Newly created projects have most APIs disabled by default; the error names the service, and enabling it on the project is the direct fix.

option_breakdown.A: The error is about a disabled service, not a quota; a quota can't be raised for an API that isn't enabled.
option_breakdown.B: Correct. Newly created projects have most APIs disabled; the error names the service, and enabling it on the project is the fix.
option_breakdown.C: A missing role produces a permission-denied error; a role doesn't enable a service.
option_breakdown.D: The error is permanent until the API is enabled, so retries keep failing.

questions.title: Regional CPU limit reached at peak
questions.summary: Regional CPU limits are quotas; request an increase for that quota in that region.
questions.question: A batch job in us-central1 fails at peak because the project has hit its regional CPU quota. The demand is legitimate, can't be reduced, and must run in us-central1 next to its data. What should you do?

options.A: Add exponential backoff and retries to the job's VM creation.
options.B: Create the extra VMs in a second project.
options.C: Request an increase to the regional CPU quota.
options.D: Use machine types with fewer, larger vCPUs.

explanation.summary: Regional CPU limits are quotas; when the demand is legitimate the supported remedy is to request an increase for that specific quota in that region.

option_breakdown.A: Retries wait for capacity that the quota will never allow at peak.
option_breakdown.B: Spreading across projects sidesteps the quota at the cost of a fragmented estate, which is not the supported fix.
option_breakdown.C: Correct. Regional CPU limits are quotas; when demand is legitimate, the supported remedy is to request an increase for that quota in that region.
option_breakdown.D: The quota counts vCPUs, so the same demand uses the same quota whatever the machine size.

questions.title: Intermittent 429s during short spikes
questions.summary: Rate-limit errors on brief spikes call for exponential backoff, not more quota.
questions.question: An application intermittently receives HTTP 429 responses during brief traffic spikes, but stays well within its daily allowance and its quota shows plenty of headroom. What should you do?

options.A: Enable the API again on the project.
options.B: Request a higher quota for the API.
options.C: Grant the caller a broader IAM role.
options.D: Retry with exponential backoff and jitter.

explanation.summary: Rate-limit errors on brief spikes are the documented case for exponential backoff with jitter; the underlying quota is adequate.

option_breakdown.A: The API is already enabled, or every call would fail; re-enabling changes nothing.
option_breakdown.B: The quota has headroom, so a higher one would not stop rejections during brief bursts.
option_breakdown.C: 429 means too many requests, not a permission problem; a role changes nothing.
option_breakdown.D: Correct. Rate-limit errors on brief spikes are the documented case for exponential backoff with jitter; the underlying quota is adequate.

explanation.gcloud_command:
# client-side retry; inspect limits with:
gcloud services quota list --service=SERVICE --consumer=projects/PROJECT_ID

questions.title: Permission denied with API enabled
questions.summary: With the service enabled and quota available, the remaining cause is a missing IAM binding.
questions.question: A service account receives 'Permission denied' calling an API. You have confirmed the service is enabled and the project is well under quota. What should you do?

options.A: Grant the service account a role with the missing permission, on the resource it calls.
options.B: Retry the call with exponential backoff.
options.C: Request a higher quota for the API.
options.D: Disable and re-enable the API on the project.

explanation.summary: With the service enabled and quota available, a permission denial leaves the IAM binding as the remaining cause; granting the required role on the resource resolves it.

option_breakdown.A: Correct. With the service enabled and quota available, a permission denial leaves the IAM binding as the cause; granting a role that holds the permission on the resource resolves it.
option_breakdown.B: A permission denial is not transient; every retry is denied the same way.
option_breakdown.C: Quota errors return 429 or RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED; this caller is under quota.
option_breakdown.D: The API is enabled, and re-enabling it grants no permissions.

questions.title: Pipeline prerequisite for a fresh project
questions.summary: Service enablement is an idempotent prerequisite that belongs at the start of the pipeline.
questions.question: Before a Terraform run can create Cloud Run services in a fresh project, the pipeline must guarantee the necessary services are available, and the step must be safe to run on every execution. What should the pipeline do first?

options.A: Grant the pipeline's service account roles/owner on the project.
options.B: Run gcloud services enable for the APIs it needs as its first step.
options.C: Ask an administrator to enable the APIs in the console before each run.
options.D: Retry the Terraform run until the services become available.

explanation.summary: Enabling an API is idempotent — it succeeds whether or not the API is already on — so it is safe on every run and guarantees the prerequisite. (Terraform's google_project_service does the same declaratively.)

option_breakdown.A: Owner would let the pipeline enable APIs but does not enable them, and it is far broader than needed.
option_breakdown.B: Correct. Enabling an API is idempotent — it succeeds whether or not the API is already on — so it is safe on every run and guarantees the prerequisite. (Terraform's google_project_service does the same declaratively.)
option_breakdown.C: A manual console step is not repeatable and cannot be guaranteed on every execution.
option_breakdown.D: A disabled API never becomes available by itself; retrying only repeats the failure.

explanation.gcloud_command: gcloud services enable run.googleapis.com artifactregistry.googleapis.com cloudbuild.googleapis.com

questions.title: Survive one data centre failure
questions.summary: Zones are independent failure domains inside a region; a regional MIG spreads instances across them.
questions.question: A web tier must stay available if a single Google Cloud data centre fails. The business explicitly accepts an outage if an entire region is lost, and wants to avoid cross-region cost and latency. What should you do?

options.A: Deploy across two or more regions.
options.B: Deploy into a single zone.
options.C: Deploy across multiple zones in one region.
options.D: Deploy a zonal managed instance group with autohealing.

explanation.summary: Zones are independent failure domains inside a region, so spreading instances across zones — via a regional managed instance group — survives a zonal failure at no cross-region latency cost.

option_breakdown.A: It survives a zone loss too, but adds the cross-region cost and latency the business wants to avoid.
option_breakdown.B: A single zone has no redundancy, so one data centre failure takes the tier down.
option_breakdown.C: Correct. Zones are independent failure domains inside a region, so spreading instances across zones, for example with a regional managed instance group, survives a zonal failure with no cross-region latency.
option_breakdown.D: Autohealing recreates instances in the same zone, so it doesn't help when that zone is down.

explanation.gcloud_command:
gcloud compute instance-groups managed create web-mig \
  --template=web-tpl --size=6 --region=us-central1

questions.title: Survive the loss of a whole region
questions.summary: Only a deployment spanning more than one region survives a regional outage.
questions.question: A service must keep serving even if an entire Google Cloud region becomes unavailable. What deployment shape meets the requirement?

options.A: Deploy in one region, with snapshots stored in a multi-region location.
options.B: Deploy across multiple zones in one region.
options.C: Deploy into a single zone.
options.D: Deploy across multiple regions.

explanation.summary: Only a deployment spanning more than one region survives the loss of a region; zonal redundancy inside one region cannot.

option_breakdown.A: Snapshots let you rebuild elsewhere later, but the service stops serving until you do.
option_breakdown.B: Multiple zones survive the loss of a data centre, not of the whole region.
option_breakdown.C: A single zone fails with its zone, let alone its region.
option_breakdown.D: Correct. Only a deployment spanning more than one region survives the loss of a region; zonal redundancy inside one region cannot.

questions.title: Confirm a machine family exists in a new country
questions.summary: Product and machine-type availability varies by region and zone and must be verified first.
questions.question: The team plans a design around the C3 machine family in a region where the company has never deployed. Before the design depends on it, you need to know whether C3 is offered in that region's zones. What should you check?

options.A: The machine types listed for each zone in that region.
options.B: The project's Compute Engine quotas for that region.
options.C: The organisation policy for allowed resource locations.
options.D: The project's list of enabled APIs.

explanation.summary: Machine families are offered per zone, and not every zone has every family. Listing the machine types available in each of the region's zones answers the question.

option_breakdown.A: Correct. Machine types are listed per zone, so this shows directly whether C3 is offered in that region.
option_breakdown.B: Quotas say how much you may use, not which machine families exist in a zone.
option_breakdown.C: The policy says where you're allowed to create resources, not what Google offers there.
option_breakdown.D: Enabled APIs say which services you can call, not where hardware is available.

explanation.gcloud_command: gcloud compute machine-types list --filter="zone~^europe-west10 AND name~^c3-"

questions.title: Latency for users on two continents
questions.summary: Serving each population from a nearby region removes the transatlantic round trip.
questions.question: Users in Europe and North America both report high latency against a service hosted in a single US region. What should you do?

options.A: Add a second zone in the existing US region.
options.B: Add a European region behind a global external Application Load Balancer.
options.C: Move the service to a larger machine type.
options.D: Switch the service to Standard Tier networking.

explanation.summary: Serving Europe from a European region removes the transatlantic round trip, and the global load balancer's anycast IP sends each user to the nearest healthy backend.

option_breakdown.A: A second zone in the same region is still across the Atlantic from European users.
option_breakdown.B: Correct. Serving Europe from a European region removes the transatlantic round trip, and the global load balancer's anycast IP sends each user to the nearest healthy backend.
option_breakdown.C: More CPU does not shorten the distance packets travel.
option_breakdown.D: Standard Tier routes over the public internet and is regional only — it tends to add latency, and it cannot front backends in two regions.

questions.title: Disposable batch experiment
questions.summary: When work is disposable and re-runnable, single-zone placement avoids paying for redundancy.
questions.question: A short-lived batch experiment must run as cheaply as possible. If it fails it can simply be re-run, and no redundancy is required. What should you do?

options.A: Deploy into a single zone with a zonal reservation.
options.B: Deploy across multiple zones in one region.
options.C: Deploy into a single zone.
options.D: Deploy across multiple regions.

explanation.summary: When the workload is disposable and re-runnable, single-zone placement avoids the cost of redundancy that the requirement explicitly does not need.

option_breakdown.A: A reservation bills for the capacity whether or not it is used, which adds cost for no benefit here.
option_breakdown.B: Spreading across zones buys redundancy that the experiment doesn't need.
option_breakdown.C: Correct. When the workload is disposable and can be re-run, single-zone placement avoids the cost of redundancy the requirement doesn't need.
option_breakdown.D: Multiple regions add the most cost and complexity, for redundancy nobody asked for.

questions.title: Find every VM with an external IP now
questions.subtopic: Asset Inventory and Gemini Cloud Assist
questions.summary: Asset search queries live resource metadata org-wide in one call.
questions.question: Security asks, right now, for a list of every Compute Engine instance in the organisation that has an external IP address. What should you do?

options.A: Export Cloud Asset Inventory snapshots to BigQuery and query them.
options.B: Create a Cloud Asset Inventory feed that publishes asset changes to Pub/Sub.
options.C: Query Cloud Logging for the relevant audit log entries.
options.D: Use Cloud Asset Inventory to search all resources across the organisation.

explanation.summary: The Cloud Asset Inventory search API queries live resource metadata across the whole organisation in one call, which is the fastest way to answer an ad-hoc inventory question.

option_breakdown.A: It works, but needs an export and a query; the search API answers this one-off question directly.
option_breakdown.B: A feed reports future changes; it doesn't list what exists now.
option_breakdown.C: Audit logs record actions and age out; they are not an inventory of current instances.
option_breakdown.D: Correct. The Cloud Asset Inventory search API queries live resource metadata across the whole organisation in one call, which answers an ad-hoc inventory question quickest.

questions.title: Two years of monthly configuration snapshots
questions.subtopic: Asset Inventory and Gemini Cloud Assist
questions.summary: Asset snapshot export to BigQuery produces the durable, queryable historical record.
questions.question: Compliance needs a point-in-time record of every resource and IAM policy each month, retained and analysable for two years. What should you configure?

options.A: Monthly Cloud Asset Inventory exports to BigQuery.
options.B: Admin Activity audit logs in Cloud Logging.
options.C: Cloud Asset Inventory asset history (get-history).
options.D: Cloud Asset Inventory search across the organisation.

explanation.summary: Exporting asset snapshots to BigQuery produces the durable, queryable historical record that a retention and analysis requirement needs.

option_breakdown.A: Correct. Exporting asset snapshots to BigQuery each month produces the durable, queryable point-in-time record that two years of retention needs.
option_breakdown.B: Audit logs record changes, not a full snapshot of every resource, and their default retention is shorter than two years.
option_breakdown.C: Asset history covers only the last five weeks.
option_breakdown.D: Search shows the current state only, not what existed a year ago.

questions.title: Detect an open firewall rule within seconds
questions.subtopic: Asset Inventory and Gemini Cloud Assist
questions.summary: A real-time asset feed publishes each asset change to Pub/Sub as it happens.
questions.question: After an incident at Tamsin Robotics, the security team must be alerted within seconds whenever any project in the organization creates or changes a VPC firewall rule, so that a rule allowing 0.0.0.0/0 is caught as it appears. What should you configure?

options.A: Search Cloud Asset Inventory for open firewall rules.
options.B: A Cloud Asset Inventory feed that publishes firewall changes to Pub/Sub.
options.C: A daily Cloud Asset Inventory export to BigQuery.
options.D: Firewall Insights for the organisation's networks.

explanation.summary: A real-time asset feed publishes each asset change to Pub/Sub as it happens, which is the only option that meets a seconds-level detection requirement.

option_breakdown.A: A search answers when someone runs it; nobody is notified when a rule appears.
option_breakdown.B: Correct. A real-time asset feed publishes each firewall change to Pub/Sub as it happens, which meets a seconds-level requirement.
option_breakdown.C: A daily export finds the rule up to a day later.
option_breakdown.D: Firewall Insights analyses rule usage and overly permissive rules over time; it isn't a real-time change notification.

questions.title: Locate a bucket by partial name
questions.subtopic: Asset Inventory and Gemini Cloud Assist
questions.summary: Asset search matches resources by name fragment across the organisation.
questions.question: An engineer needs to find which project owns a Cloud Storage bucket, knowing only part of its name. What should they do?

options.A: Run gcloud storage ls in every project until the bucket appears.
options.B: Search Admin Activity audit logs for bucket creation events.
options.C: Read the billing export for the storage SKU charges.
options.D: Search Cloud Asset Inventory across the organisation for the name fragment.

explanation.summary: gcloud asset search-all-resources (or the console's Asset Inventory search) matches a name fragment across the organisation and returns the full resource name, including the project.

option_breakdown.A: Listing project by project is slow and needs access to each project; it is the manual version of a search the platform already provides.
option_breakdown.B: Audit logs are kept for a limited time and record changes; a bucket created years ago may not appear.
option_breakdown.C: Billing data is aggregated by project and SKU, not by bucket name.
option_breakdown.D: Correct. gcloud asset search-all-resources (or the console's Asset Inventory search) matches a name fragment across the organisation and returns the full resource name, including the project.

questions.title: Centralise logs from every project
questions.summary: An aggregated sink at the org or folder node routes descendants' logs to one destination.
questions.question: Security wants every project's logs delivered into one central location for retention and search, configured once at the organisation level rather than per project. What should you do?

options.A: Install the Ops Agent on the virtual machines.
options.B: Create an organisation-level aggregated sink that routes to one log bucket.
options.C: Configure a metrics scope in one project and add the other projects to it.
options.D: View each project's dashboards separately in its own Cloud Monitoring page.

explanation.summary: An aggregated sink created at the organisation or folder node, with the include-children flag, routes logs from every descendant project to a single destination and keeps working for projects created later.

option_breakdown.A: The Ops Agent collects guest-level metrics and logs from VMs; it does not consolidate anything across projects.
option_breakdown.B: Correct. An aggregated sink created at the organisation or folder node, with the include-children flag, routes logs from every descendant project to a single destination and keeps working for projects created later.
option_breakdown.C: A metrics scope lets one project view other projects' metrics; logs stay where they are.
option_breakdown.D: Viewing projects one by one is the current situation, not central retention.

questions.title: Console access for an external workforce
questions.summary: A workforce pool federates human identities for interactive Google Cloud access.
questions.question: Employees of an acquired company must sign in to the Google Cloud console using their existing corporate IdP credentials, with no Cloud Identity accounts created for them. What should you configure?

options.A: Configure Workload Identity Federation with a workload identity pool and provider.
options.B: Create service account keys and distribute them to the external system.
options.C: Create a Cloud Identity account for every external user.
options.D: Configure Workforce Identity Federation with a workforce pool and provider.

explanation.summary: Workforce Identity Federation federates human identities from an external IdP into Google Cloud, giving console and gcloud access through a workforce pool without provisioning Cloud Identity accounts.

option_breakdown.A: Workload Identity Federation is for *machine* identities from an external system; it does not give employees interactive console access.
option_breakdown.B: Downloadable keys are long-lived credentials that never expire and are the leading cause of credential compromise.
option_breakdown.C: Provisioning accounts for large external populations is exactly the cost and administrative burden federation removes.
option_breakdown.D: Correct. Workforce Identity Federation federates human identities from an external IdP into Google Cloud, giving console and gcloud access through a workforce pool without provisioning Cloud Identity accounts.

explanation.gcloud_command:
gcloud iam workforce-pools providers create-oidc corp \
  --workforce-pool=acquired-pool --location=global \
  --issuer-uri='https://idp.example.com' --client-id=CLIENT_ID

questions.title: An organisation without a domain for a new Free Trial customer
questions.summary: New Free Trial sign-ups get a standalone organisation automatically; the signing-up user becomes Organization Owner.
questions.question: A two-person startup signs up for Google Cloud for the first time on a new Free Trial. They own no company domain and have no Cloud Identity or Google Workspace account, but want folders, organisation policies and organisation-level IAM from the first day. What gives them an organisation resource?

options.A: Buy a domain, verify it in Cloud Identity Free, and wait for the organisation to be created from it.
options.B: Use the standalone organisation created with the new Free Trial sign-up.
options.C: Create a top-level folder in the console, which becomes the organisation node for the account.
options.D: Open a support case asking Google to provision an organisation for their Gmail account.

explanation.summary: A standalone organisation gives a new Free Trial customer a real resource hierarchy — folders, organisation policies, organisation-level IAM — without a verified domain or a Cloud Identity super administrator. It is created automatically at sign-up and the user who signed up becomes Organization Owner.

option_breakdown.A: Verifying a domain works, but they own no domain; the guide's standalone route exists precisely for this case.
option_breakdown.B: Correct. A standalone organisation is created for a new Free Trial sign-up with no domain: it is named after the user, who becomes its Organization Owner, and others join by invitation.
option_breakdown.C: Folders live under an organisation; creating one never creates the organisation itself.
option_breakdown.D: Organisations are not provisioned by support request; they come from Cloud Identity/Workspace or a standalone sign-up.

explanation.gcloud_command: gcloud organizations list   # the standalone organisation appears, named after the user

questions.title: A second owner for a standalone organisation
questions.summary: Standalone org owners are Google accounts added by invitation they must accept; a service account cannot be an owner.
questions.question: In a standalone organisation, the founder wants a colleague who uses a personal Google account to share Organization Owner duties. They also propose making the CI pipeline's service account an owner as a backup in case both people are unavailable. What should they do?

options.A: Grant roles/owner on the organisation to both the colleague and the service account; both take effect immediately.
options.B: Create a Cloud Identity user for the colleague, since standalone organisations only accept managed users.
options.C: Invite the colleague, who must accept, and drop the service account plan.
options.D: Add both principals to a workforce identity pool, which makes every pool member an owner automatically.

explanation.summary: People join a standalone organisation by invitation, which they must accept (within 30 days). Ownership must always rest with at least one active Google account; service accounts can never hold the Organization Owner position, so the backup plan has to be a second human owner.

option_breakdown.A: The service account cannot become an organisation owner, and the colleague's access starts only when they accept.
option_breakdown.B: Standalone organisations exist for customers without Cloud Identity; they hold Google accounts and workforce pool principals.
option_breakdown.C: Correct. Inviting a second person, who accepts, is the supported way to share ownership; a service account can never be an organisation owner.
option_breakdown.D: Workforce identity pools federate sign-in from an external IdP; membership grants no role on its own.

explanation.gcloud_command: # Console > IAM & Admin > Organization > Invite members

questions.title: A guided foundation with a Shared VPC host, deployable as Terraform
questions.summary: Google Cloud Setup is the console's guided flow for a new organisation's foundation, including a Shared VPC network.
questions.question: A company's new organisation needs its foundation: administrator groups, a folder structure, a Shared VPC host project with subnets, central logging and monitoring, and a baseline of security organisation policies. The team wants a guided, console-based flow that follows Google's recommendations and can either deploy directly or hand them the result as Terraform. What should they use?

options.A: Application Design Center, starting from its web-application template.
options.B: A Deployment Manager template library, deployed once per folder.
options.C: An auto-mode VPC created in every project, with firewall rules copied between projects.
options.D: The Google Cloud Setup guided flow in the console.

explanation.summary: Google Cloud Setup walks an administrator through identity and groups, administrative access, billing, the folder hierarchy, a starter network (a Shared VPC host with subnets), central logging and monitoring, and recommended security policies. It can apply the result or export it as Terraform to keep in version control.

option_breakdown.A: Application Design Center builds application architectures from approved templates; it does not create an organisation's foundation.
option_breakdown.B: Deployment Manager is deprecated and offers no guided foundation flow.
option_breakdown.C: Per-project auto-mode networks are the opposite of a central, planned foundation network.
option_breakdown.D: Correct. It is the console's built-in foundation flow, and it can export Terraform.

explanation.gcloud_command: # Console > Google Cloud Setup   (deploy directly or download as Terraform)

questions.title: Plain-language questions about your own resources
questions.subtopic: Asset Inventory and Gemini Cloud Assist
questions.summary: Gemini Cloud Assist answers natural-language questions about your resources inside the console, with your permissions.
questions.question: An operations lead who does not use the command line wants to ask, from the Google Cloud console and in plain language, which Compute Engine VMs in a project have an external IP address and no 'owner' label. What should they use?

options.A: Gemini Cloud Assist in the console.
options.B: Cloud Hub's application health view.
options.C: A Looker Studio report built over the billing export.
options.D: Personalized Service Health.

explanation.summary: Gemini Cloud Assist is the AI assistant built into the console: it can analyse your own resources and configuration in natural language (drawing on Cloud Asset Inventory data) and suggest the gcloud command or query behind the answer. It sees only what the asking user is allowed to see.

option_breakdown.A: Correct. It is designed for exactly this kind of question about your own estate.
option_breakdown.B: Cloud Hub shows application health, incidents and deployments, not ad-hoc questions about resource configuration.
option_breakdown.C: The billing export has cost rows, not network configuration or complete label state for unbilled attributes.
option_breakdown.D: Personalized Service Health reports Google Cloud incidents affecting you, not your resources' settings.

questions.title: Who can reach this bucket, through groups and inheritance
questions.subtopic: Asset Inventory and Gemini Cloud Assist
questions.summary: Policy Analyzer (Cloud Asset Inventory) expands groups and inherited bindings to answer who has access to a resource.
questions.question: A security reviewer must list every principal who can read objects in one Cloud Storage bucket, including access that comes from group membership and from roles granted on the project, folder or organisation above it. What should you use?

options.A: The bucket's own IAM policy.
options.B: Data Access audit logs for the bucket over the last 30 days.
options.C: The IAM role recommender for the project.
options.D: Policy Analyzer, with group expansion.

explanation.summary: A resource's own IAM policy shows only direct bindings. Policy Analyzer, part of Cloud Asset Inventory, evaluates the whole hierarchy and expands groups, so it answers 'who can access this resource, and why'.

option_breakdown.A: The bucket's policy omits bindings inherited from above and doesn't expand groups.
option_breakdown.B: Audit logs show who did read, not who can read.
option_breakdown.C: Role recommendations suggest reducing grants; they do not enumerate access to one resource.
option_breakdown.D: Correct. Policy Analyzer in Cloud Asset Inventory evaluates inherited bindings and group membership together, for a permission such as storage.objects.get on the bucket.

questions.title: Organisation-wide asset search denied to a project owner
questions.subtopic: Asset Inventory and Gemini Cloud Assist
questions.summary: Searching assets across the organisation needs Cloud Asset Viewer at the organisation node, not project roles.
questions.question: An engineer who is Owner on several projects runs `gcloud asset search-all-resources --scope=organizations/ORG_ID` and receives a permission error. They need read-only search across the whole organisation. What should you grant?

options.A: roles/owner on every project in the organisation.
options.B: roles/cloudasset.viewer on the organisation node.
options.C: roles/resourcemanager.organizationAdmin on the organisation node.
options.D: roles/browser on the organisation node.

explanation.summary: A search's scope determines where permission is checked. Searching at organisation scope needs cloudasset.assets.searchAllResources on the organisation, which Cloud Asset Viewer grants read-only. Project roles never add up to an organisation-level permission.

option_breakdown.A: Project roles cannot satisfy a check made on the organisation node, and this over-grants massively.
option_breakdown.B: Correct. It is the read-only role that carries the asset search permissions, granted where the search is scoped.
option_breakdown.C: Organization Administrator manages IAM for the whole organisation — far more than read-only search.
option_breakdown.D: Browser shows the hierarchy but does not include the Cloud Asset Inventory search permissions.

questions.title: Adding one binding without disturbing the rest
questions.summary: add-iam-policy-binding adds a single binding safely; set-iam-policy replaces the whole policy.
questions.question: A provisioning script at Juniper Health must give the group data-eng@example.com the BigQuery Data Viewer role on project analytics-prod. Three other teams change that project's IAM policy through their own automation during the day, and none of their bindings may be lost. Which command should the script run?

options.A: Run set-iam-policy with a file that holds only the new binding.
options.B: Run get-iam-policy and email the output to the project owner.
options.C: Run add-iam-policy-binding for the group and the role.
options.D: Create a custom role with the BigQuery viewer permissions.

explanation.summary: add-iam-policy-binding performs a read-modify-write of the policy for you and adds exactly one binding, leaving every other team's bindings untouched.

option_breakdown.A: set-iam-policy replaces the entire policy, so a file with one binding deletes every other binding in the project.
option_breakdown.B: Reading the policy grants nothing; a manual hand-off is not what a script is for.
option_breakdown.C: Correct. add-iam-policy-binding reads, modifies and writes the policy for you, adding exactly one binding and leaving other teams' bindings untouched.
option_breakdown.D: Creating a custom role grants it to nobody, and a predefined role already fits.

questions.title: Letting a team deploy Cloud Run in one project
questions.summary: Grant the narrow predefined role for the task, to a group, on the one project — not a basic role.
questions.question: The payments team must be able to deploy and update Cloud Run services in project pay-prod, and nothing else in that project. Team membership changes every month. What should you grant?

options.A: roles/editor on pay-prod to each member of the team individually.
options.B: roles/run.admin at the organisation node to the group payments-devs@example.com.
options.C: roles/owner on pay-prod to the team lead, who then deploys for everyone.
options.D: roles/run.developer on pay-prod to the group payments-devs@example.com.

explanation.summary: Cloud Run Developer covers deploying and updating services; binding it to a group on the one project follows least privilege and absorbs membership changes without IAM edits.

option_breakdown.A: Editor spans every service in the project, and per-user bindings churn with every joiner and leaver.
option_breakdown.B: An organisation binding reaches every project in the company, far beyond pay-prod.
option_breakdown.C: Owner is broader than any need here, and routing every deployment through one person is not access management.
option_breakdown.D: Correct. Cloud Run Developer covers deploying and updating services; binding it to a group on the one project follows least privilege and absorbs membership changes without IAM edits.

questions.title: A two-year-old account that now wants folders
questions.summary: Standalone organisations are only for new Free Trial customers; an existing customer with a domain uses Cloud Identity.
questions.question: A company has run a dozen projects on Google Cloud for two years without an organisation resource. It owns the domain kestrel.io, does not use Google Workspace, and now wants folders and organisation policies. What should it do?

options.A: Request a standalone organisation for the existing account from the console.
options.B: Create a folder named kestrel.io, which becomes the organisation node for the account.
options.C: Sign up for Cloud Identity Free, verify kestrel.io, then move the projects in.
options.D: Enable the Resource Manager API in each project, which creates the organisation automatically.

explanation.summary: An existing customer with a domain gets an organisation through Cloud Identity (or Workspace): verify the domain, and the organisation resource is created; existing projects can then be moved under it.

option_breakdown.A: Standalone organisations are created only for new Free Trial sign-ups, not for existing accounts.
option_breakdown.B: A folder always lives under an organisation; it can never be one.
option_breakdown.C: Correct. An existing customer with a domain gets an organisation through Cloud Identity (or Workspace): verify the domain, and the organisation resource is created; existing projects can then be moved under it.
option_breakdown.D: Enabling an API never creates an organisation resource.

explanation.gcloud_command:
gcloud organizations list
gcloud beta projects move PROJECT_ID --organization=ORG_ID

questions.title: An invitation to a standalone organisation that lapsed
questions.summary: Invitations to a standalone organisation must be accepted within 30 days; after that, invite again.
questions.question: The founder of a standalone organisation invited a co-founder's Google account as an Organization Owner six weeks ago. The co-founder never accepted and now cannot see the organisation. What should the founder do?

options.A: Grant roles/owner on each project to the co-founder instead; organisation roles do not apply to standalone organisations.
options.B: Wait: the invitation stays open until the co-founder signs in.
options.C: Create a second standalone organisation under the co-founder's account and link the two.
options.D: Send a new invitation, which the co-founder must accept within 30 days.

explanation.summary: People join a standalone organisation by an invitation they must accept within 30 days; an expired invitation is simply sent again.

option_breakdown.A: Standalone organisations support organisation-level IAM; project grants would also miss future projects.
option_breakdown.B: Invitations expire after 30 days.
option_breakdown.C: Organisations cannot be linked, and a second one splits the environment.
option_breakdown.D: Correct. People join a standalone organisation by an invitation they must accept within 30 days; an expired invitation is simply sent again.

explanation.gcloud_command: # Console > IAM & Admin > Organization > Invite members

questions.title: No default network in any new project
questions.summary: compute.skipDefaultNetworkCreation stops the permissive default VPC from being created in new projects.
questions.question: The security baseline for a new organisation says no project may ever start with the auto-mode default network and its permissive firewall rules. Projects are created by many teams. What should you configure once?

options.A: Enforce compute.skipDefaultNetworkCreation on the organisation.
options.B: Ask each team to delete the default network after creating a project.
options.C: A hierarchical firewall policy that denies all ingress at the organisation.
options.D: Disable the Compute Engine API in every new project.

explanation.summary: The boolean constraint compute.skipDefaultNetworkCreation prevents the default network from being created when the Compute Engine API is enabled, for every project beneath the node where it is enforced.

option_breakdown.A: Correct. The boolean constraint compute.skipDefaultNetworkCreation prevents the default network from being created when the Compute Engine API is enabled, for every project beneath the node where it is enforced.
option_breakdown.B: A manual clean-up step will be missed, and the network exists in the meantime.
option_breakdown.C: A deny-all firewall policy blocks traffic but the default network is still created.
option_breakdown.D: Without the Compute Engine API, teams cannot create VMs at all.

explanation.gcloud_command:
gcloud org-policies set-policy skip-default-net.yaml
# name: organizations/ORG_ID/policies/compute.skipDefaultNetworkCreation, rules: - enforce: true

questions.title: Where the shared foundation network lives
questions.summary: A foundation network is a Shared VPC in a dedicated host project, with workload projects attached.
questions.question: You are setting up networking for a new organisation. A central network team will own subnets, routes and firewall policy for all environments, while application teams keep their own projects and budgets. Where should the network be created?

options.A: In each application team's project, peered with every other application project.
options.B: In the largest application project, which the network team is added to as Owner.
options.C: In the organisation node itself, which holds networks for every project.
options.D: In a dedicated Shared VPC host project, with app projects attached.

explanation.summary: A dedicated Shared VPC host project separates network ownership from workload ownership: the network team administers one network, and service projects consume its subnets.

option_breakdown.A: A full mesh of peerings gives many networks to administer and is non-transitive.
option_breakdown.B: Hosting the network in an application project mixes ownership and gives the network team rights over that team's workloads.
option_breakdown.C: Networks belong to projects; the organisation node cannot hold a VPC.
option_breakdown.D: Correct. A dedicated Shared VPC host project separates network ownership from workload ownership: the network team administers one network, and service projects consume its subnets.

explanation.gcloud_command:
gcloud compute shared-vpc enable net-host-prod
gcloud compute shared-vpc associated-projects add app-1 \
  --host-project=net-host-prod

questions.title: Granting a role to a federated group
questions.summary: Federated groups are granted roles with a principalSet identifier naming the workforce pool and group.
questions.question: Engineers sign in through a workforce identity pool named corp-pool, whose provider maps Entra ID group IDs to google.groups. Members of the Entra ID group with ID a1b2c3 must get Viewer on project ops-prod. Which member should the binding use?

options.A: A group: member made from the Entra ID group ID.
options.B: A serviceAccount: member named after the workforce pool.
