option_breakdown.D: A shared service account hides who acted and isn't needed for a federated user.

questions.title: A firewall rule's settings from two months ago
questions.subtopic: Asset Inventory and Gemini Cloud Assist
questions.summary: Cloud Asset Inventory history covers about five weeks; older configuration changes are found in Admin Activity audit logs, which are kept for 400 days.
questions.question: An auditor at Harrow Bank asks what the firewall rule allow-partner allowed eight weeks ago, before two changes were made to it. No asset exports or feeds were ever set up, and no log sinks exist. Where can you find the changes?

options.A: The rule's asset history in Cloud Asset Inventory.
options.B: Firewall Rules Logging for the rule.
options.C: VPC Flow Logs from that period.
options.D: The Admin Activity audit log entries for the rule.

explanation.summary: Admin Activity audit logs record every change to a firewall rule, with the request, and are kept for 400 days. Asset history covers only the last five weeks.

option_breakdown.A: Asset history reaches back about five weeks, so eight weeks ago is out of range.
option_breakdown.B: Firewall Rules Logging records connections the rule matched, not changes to its configuration.
option_breakdown.C: Flow logs record traffic samples and must have been enabled at the time.
option_breakdown.D: Correct. The rule's patch and update entries in Admin Activity logs show what changed and when, for 400 days.

questions.title: No one may delete the network host project
questions.summary: An IAM deny policy denying cloudresourcemanager.googleapis.com/projects.delete stops anyone, Owners included, from deleting a project.
questions.question: Deleting the Shared VPC host project at Ingram Logistics would take down every service project's network. Several administrators hold Owner on it. Using generally available features only, how do you stop anyone from deleting the project, Owners included?

options.A: Remove the Owner role from everyone and grant Editor instead.
options.B: A deny policy on the project that denies the projects.delete permission.
options.C: An organisation policy that restricts resource locations for the project.
options.D: A budget with a 100% threshold that alerts the network team.

explanation.summary: Deny policies are evaluated before allow policies, so a deny rule for cloudresourcemanager.googleapis.com/projects.delete blocks deletion whatever roles a principal holds.

option_breakdown.A: Editor can't delete a project, but removing Owner from everyone also removes the administrators' ability to run the project.
option_breakdown.B: Correct. A deny rule on projects.delete stops every principal it names, including Owners, and it is GA.
option_breakdown.C: A location policy limits where resources are created, not whether the project can be deleted.
option_breakdown.D: A budget watches spending; it can't block an action.

questions.title: US workloads that need FedRAMP High controls
questions.summary: Assured Workloads applies a regulatory control package, such as FedRAMP High, to a folder: US data location, US-person support personnel and allowed services.
questions.question: A contractor at Halsey Federal will host a US government system that must meet FedRAMP High: data stored only in the United States, support access only by US persons with enhanced background checks, and only services authorised at that level. What should you set up?

options.A: An Assured Workloads folder with the FedRAMP High control package.
options.B: The gcp.resourceLocations organisation policy set to in:us-locations.
options.C: A VPC Service Controls perimeter around the system's projects.
options.D: Access Transparency logs reviewed weekly by the security team.

explanation.summary: Assured Workloads' FedRAMP High package enforces US data location, restricts support personnel and limits the folder to authorised services, and it monitors for violations.

option_breakdown.A: Correct. The control package covers data location, personnel access and service restrictions together.
option_breakdown.B: A location policy covers where data lives, not who at Google may access it or which services are authorised.
option_breakdown.C: A perimeter limits data movement through Google APIs; it doesn't control location or personnel.
option_breakdown.D: Access Transparency shows access after it happens; it doesn't restrict who can access.

questions.title: A project outside the Assured Workloads folder
questions.summary: Assured Workloads controls apply to the projects in its folder; a project created elsewhere in the organisation gets none of them.
questions.question: Corwen Health created an Assured Workloads folder with the EU Data Boundary and Support package. A team then created a project directly under the organisation and deployed patient data to us-central1 without any error. Why was nothing blocked?

options.A: The package only alerts on violations and never blocks anything.
options.B: The package's controls take 30 days to start applying.
options.C: The controls apply only to projects in the Assured Workloads folder.
options.D: us-central1 is allowed by the EU Data Boundary package for backups.

explanation.summary: Assured Workloads enforces its package with organisation policies on its folder, so only projects created inside that folder inherit the controls.

option_breakdown.A: The package enforces controls such as resource locations through organisation policies, and also monitors for violations.
option_breakdown.B: Controls apply as soon as the folder exists; there is no waiting period.
option_breakdown.C: Correct. A project at the organisation root inherits nothing from the folder, so EU-only locations didn't apply to it.
option_breakdown.D: The EU packages restrict resources to EU locations; us-central1 is outside them.

questions.title: Finding out when an Assured Workloads control is overridden
questions.summary: Assured Workloads monitors its folder for organisation policy and resource violations and can email notifications when they happen.
questions.question: An administrator at Lyle Defence with Organization Policy Administrator could change a policy inside the company's Assured Workloads folder. The compliance team wants to know whenever such a change breaks the control package, without building anything. What should you use?

options.A: A budget alert on the folder's projects.
options.B: Assured Workloads violation monitoring, with email notifications.
options.C: A Cloud Asset Inventory export to BigQuery every month.
options.D: Personalized Service Health alerts for the folder.

explanation.summary: Assured Workloads watches its folder for changes that break the package's organisation policies or resource rules, lists them as violations and can notify by email.

option_breakdown.A: Budgets watch spending, not policy changes.
option_breakdown.B: Correct. Violation monitoring reports policy and resource violations in the folder and sends notifications.
option_breakdown.C: A monthly export is a snapshot to analyse later, not a notification when a control is broken.
option_breakdown.D: Personalized Service Health reports Google Cloud incidents, not your own policy changes.

questions.title: Where a Spanner configuration keeps its replicas
questions.summary: Describing a Spanner instance configuration lists its replicas, their types and regions, and its default leader region.
questions.question: An architect at Selby Payments is choosing a Spanner multi-region configuration. Before deciding, they need to know which regions hold read-write replicas and which region is the default leader in the configuration eur5. What is the most direct way to find out?

options.A: List the Compute Engine zones in each European region.
options.B: Create a test instance in eur5 and read its monitoring charts.
options.C: Describe the eur5 instance configuration.
options.D: Read the Spanner API's quota page for the project.

explanation.summary: An instance configuration lists its replicas with their types and locations and its default leader. Describing it answers the question without creating anything.

option_breakdown.A: Zones say where Compute Engine runs, not where a Spanner configuration places replicas.
option_breakdown.B: A test instance costs money and still doesn't show the configuration's replica layout directly.
option_breakdown.C: Correct. gcloud spanner instance-configs describe eur5 shows each replica's type and region and the default leader.
option_breakdown.D: Quotas limit capacity; they say nothing about replica placement.

questions.title: Where namespace costs appear after cost allocation
questions.summary: With GKE cost allocation enabled, namespace and Kubernetes label costs appear in the detailed usage cost export to BigQuery.
questions.question: Finance at Hawley Insurance enabled GKE cost allocation on a shared cluster. It now wants to query cost by Kubernetes namespace with SQL. Where should it look?

options.A: The standard usage cost export to BigQuery.
options.B: The detailed usage cost export to BigQuery.
options.C: The cluster's Workloads page in the console.
options.D: A budget scoped to the cluster's project.

explanation.summary: Cost allocation adds namespace and Kubernetes label information to resource-level rows, which only the detailed usage cost export contains.

option_breakdown.A: The standard export aggregates by service and SKU, without the resource-level rows cost allocation adds to.
option_breakdown.B: Correct. The detailed export carries the namespace and label breakdown that SQL can group by.
option_breakdown.C: The Workloads page shows resource requests and status, not billed cost.
option_breakdown.D: A budget alerts on a total; it doesn't break cost down by namespace.

questions.title: Why the bill went up, without SQL
questions.summary: Cloud Billing reports chart cost by project, service or SKU over time and compare periods, with no SQL; Billing Account Viewer is enough to see them.
questions.question: A manager at Thursby Media has Billing Account Viewer and asks why last month's bill was 30% higher than the month before, and which projects and services drove it. They don't write SQL, and only generally available features may be used. What should they use?

options.A: The detailed billing export, queried in BigQuery.
options.B: A budget with alerts at 50%, 90% and 100%.
options.C: Cloud Billing reports, grouped by project and then by service, comparing the two months.
options.D: The Cost Table filtered by invoice month, exported to CSV.

explanation.summary: Billing reports chart cost over time grouped by project, service or SKU, and can compare periods, so the manager sees what grew without writing queries.

option_breakdown.A: The export answers the question but needs SQL, which the manager doesn't write.
option_breakdown.B: A budget alerts about future spending; it doesn't explain last month's increase.
option_breakdown.C: Correct. Grouping the reports by project and by service shows which ones grew between the two months.
option_breakdown.D: The cost table lists invoice lines, but comparing two months in a spreadsheet is the slow way.

explanation.gcloud_command: # Console > Billing > Reports: Group by Project, then Service; time range: last two months

questions.title: One role to reorganise every folder
questions.summary: Folder Admin on the organization covers creating, moving and deleting folders, their IAM, and moving projects between folders.
questions.question: Northquay Freight is restructuring its organization. Its platform lead must create, move and delete folders anywhere in the hierarchy, change IAM on those folders, and move projects between them. She must not be able to change the organization's own allow policy. Which role should the Organization Administrator grant her on the organization?

options.A: Folder Creator (roles/resourcemanager.folderCreator)
options.B: Folder Admin (roles/resourcemanager.folderAdmin)
options.C: Organization Administrator (roles/resourcemanager.organizationAdmin)
options.D: Project Mover (roles/resourcemanager.projectMover)

explanation.summary: Folder Admin is the role for managing the folder hierarchy: it carries every folder operation, IAM on folders, and moving projects between folders, without rights over the organization's allow policy.

option_breakdown.A: Folder Creator only lets her create folders; she could not move or delete them, set their IAM or move projects.
option_breakdown.B: Correct. Folder Admin lets her create, edit, delete and move folders, change IAM on them and move projects between folders.
option_breakdown.C: Organization Administrator can also set the organization's allow policy, which Northquay explicitly rules out for her.
option_breakdown.D: Project Mover relocates projects but gives no control over the folders themselves or over folder IAM.

questions.title: A project shut down by mistake twelve days ago
questions.summary: A shut-down project stays restorable for 30 days and is brought back with gcloud projects undelete.
questions.question: Twelve days ago an engineer at Calder Optics shut down the project co-lab-tools by mistake. The console still lists the project as pending deletion, inside its 30-day recovery period. The team needs the project back with its project ID and as many of its resources as can be recovered. What should a project owner do first?

options.A: Restore the project with gcloud projects undelete
options.B: Create a new project that reuses the ID co-lab-tools
options.C: Link co-lab-tools to the Cloud Billing account again
options.D: Restore the folder that used to contain the project

explanation.summary: Shutting a project down starts a 30-day recovery period in which a project owner can restore it; only after that is the project permanently deleted.

option_breakdown.A: Correct. Within the recovery period an owner restores the project, with its ID and most resources, by undeleting it.
option_breakdown.B: A project ID is unique and permanent, so the ID cannot be given to a new project, and a new project would hold none of the resources.
option_breakdown.C: Billing does have to be linked again, but only after the restore; linking alone does not bring a project out of pending deletion.
option_breakdown.D: The folder was never deleted, so there is nothing to restore there, and restoring a folder would not restore a project inside it.

questions.title: Owner for a consultant outside the organization
questions.summary: The Owner role can be granted to a user outside the organization only from the Google Cloud console, not with the gcloud CLI.
questions.question: The project tidal-web belongs to the Harborline organization, which has no organization policy restricting the domains that can be granted roles. A handover contract requires an external consultant, whose Google Account is not part of Harborline, to hold the Owner role on the project. An engineer who is an Owner runs gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding with roles/owner for the consultant, and the command is rejected. What should the engineer do?

options.A: Apply the same binding from a policy file with gcloud projects set-iam-policy
options.B: Enable the Identity and Access Management API in tidal-web and rerun the command
options.C: Grant the consultant the Project IAM Admin role with the same gcloud command
options.D: Grant the consultant the Owner role on the IAM page of the Google Cloud console

explanation.summary: Most roles can be granted with any tool, but granting Owner on a project to a user outside the organization must be done in the Google Cloud console.

option_breakdown.A: set-iam-policy is still the gcloud CLI, and the restriction on granting Owner to an outside user applies to it as well.
option_breakdown.B: The rejection comes from the rule on Owner grants to outside users, not from a disabled API, so enabling one changes nothing.
option_breakdown.C: Project IAM Admin is a different role; the contract requires the consultant to hold Owner itself.
option_breakdown.D: Correct. Owner for a user outside the organization has to be granted through the Google Cloud console.

explanation.gcloud_command: # Console > IAM & Admin > IAM > Grant access

questions.title: Log access that ends itself on 30 June
questions.summary: A conditional role binding with an expiry time grants access that stops on its own, and it cannot be used with legacy basic roles.
questions.question: An auditor from an outside firm needs to read the application logs in the project med-claims until 30 June. Vantor Health requires the access to stop on that date without any person, script or scheduled job having to revoke it, and the auditor must get no more than log reading. What should an administrator do?

options.A: Grant Logs Viewer now, and create a Cloud Scheduler job that removes the binding
options.B: Grant the Viewer basic role with an IAM condition that expires on 30 June
options.C: Grant the Logs Viewer role with an IAM condition that expires on 30 June
options.D: Grant Logs Viewer, and shorten the auditor's session length to end on 30 June

explanation.summary: A condition on a role binding can compare request.time with a timestamp, so the binding stops granting the role at the expiry time with nothing left to clean up.

option_breakdown.A: A scheduled job is exactly what the requirement forbids, and if the job fails the access stays.
option_breakdown.B: Conditions cannot be attached to the legacy basic roles, and Viewer would also give far more than log reading.
option_breakdown.C: Correct. A conditional binding for Logs Viewer with an expiry time ends the access on the date by itself.
option_breakdown.D: Session length controls how often the auditor signs in again; after signing in, the unconditional binding still grants the role.

questions.title: Team leads who only manage access
questions.summary: Project IAM Admin lets a principal administer a project's allow policy without rights over the project's resources.
questions.question: Kestrel Robotics wants each team lead to grant and revoke roles on the team's own project, such as kr-vision. Security policy says the role a lead holds may contain only permissions for managing access: none for creating, changing or deleting resources such as VMs or buckets, and none that apply outside the project. Which grant meets these requirements for the lead of kr-vision?

options.A: Owner on the project kr-vision
options.B: Editor on the project kr-vision
options.C: Organization Administrator on the organization
options.D: Project IAM Admin on the project kr-vision

explanation.summary: Project IAM Admin (roles/resourcemanager.projectIamAdmin) carries the permissions to read and set a project's allow policy and none to manage the resources inside it.

option_breakdown.A: Owner can set the allow policy, but it also gives full control of every VM and bucket in kr-vision.
option_breakdown.B: Editor can change resources, which is forbidden, and cannot set the project's allow policy, which is required.
option_breakdown.C: A grant on the organization reaches every project under it, so the lead would have rights far outside kr-vision.
option_breakdown.D: Correct. Project IAM Admin on kr-vision lets the lead administer that project's allow policy and nothing else.

questions.title: A returning employee with a re-created account
questions.summary: A role binding for a deleted principal does not apply to a new principal with the same name; the new principal needs its own binding.
questions.question: An analyst left Orrin Analytics and her user account was deleted. Months later she returned, and because the old account could no longer be restored, an administrator created a new account with the same email address. She cannot open the project oa-reports, although its allow policy still shows her address in a Viewer binding with the prefix deleted:. What should a project administrator do?

options.A: Add a Viewer role binding for her new account to the allow policy of oa-reports
options.B: Wait for the existing Viewer binding to lose its deleted: prefix by itself
options.C: Ask the identity administrator to restore the original account that was deleted
options.D: Ask her to sign out of the console and sign in again to refresh her access

explanation.summary: A binding stays tied to the principal that was deleted. A new principal with the same name is a different principal and inherits nothing, so it must be granted the role itself.

option_breakdown.A: Correct. The old binding does not apply to the new account, so the new account needs its own Viewer binding.
option_breakdown.B: The prefix marks a principal that no longer exists; the binding never converts itself to a new account of the same name.
option_breakdown.C: The stem says the old account can no longer be restored, so this path is closed.
option_breakdown.D: Signing in again fetches the same policy, which has no binding for the new account.

questions.title: Two grants to deploy a Cloud Run revision
questions.summary: Deploying to Cloud Run needs Cloud Run Developer on the service and Service Account User on the service's identity.
questions.question: A developer at Pinecrest Media must deploy new revisions of the existing Cloud Run service encoder in the project pm-prod. The service runs as the user-managed service account encoder-run. The developer can already read the container image in Artifact Registry and holds no other roles. Following least privilege, which two grants does the developer need? (Choose two.)

options.A: Cloud Run Invoker on the service encoder
options.B: Service Account Token Creator on encoder-run
options.C: Cloud Run Developer on the service encoder
options.D: Editor on the project pm-prod

explanation.summary: A deployment changes the service, which needs Cloud Run Developer, and attaches the service's identity to the new revision, which needs Service Account User on that service account.

option_breakdown.A: Invoker lets a principal send requests to the running service; it carries no permission to deploy a revision.
option_breakdown.B: Token Creator lets the developer impersonate encoder-run, which is not what a deployment checks when it attaches the account.
option_breakdown.C: Correct. Cloud Run Developer on the service allows deploying new revisions of it.
option_breakdown.D: Editor on the whole project would be enough to deploy, but it also grants change rights on almost every resource in pm-prod.
option_breakdown.E: Correct. Service Account User on encoder-run lets the developer deploy a revision that runs as that account.

explanation.gcloud_command:
gcloud run services add-iam-policy-binding encoder --region=REGION --member="user:dev@example.com" --role="roles/run.developer"
gcloud iam service-accounts add-iam-policy-binding encoder-run@pm-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com --member="user:dev@example.com" --role="roles/iam.serviceAccountUser"

questions.title: A release engineer who only switches APIs on
questions.summary: Service Usage Admin is the narrow role for enabling and disabling services in a project.
questions.question: At Ferrowick Labs a release engineer prepares new projects by enabling the APIs each team asks for, and sometimes disabling ones no longer used. The engineer must not be able to create or change the resources those APIs manage. Following least privilege, which role should the engineer be granted on each project?

options.A: Editor (roles/editor)
options.B: Service Usage Consumer (roles/serviceusage.serviceUsageConsumer)
options.C: Service Usage Admin (roles/serviceusage.serviceUsageAdmin)
options.D: API Keys Admin (roles/serviceusage.apiKeysAdmin)

explanation.summary: Enabling and disabling services is a Service Usage operation, and Service Usage Admin is the predefined role that carries it without rights over the resources of the enabled services.

option_breakdown.A: Editor can enable services, but it can also create and change nearly every resource in the project.
option_breakdown.B: Service Usage Consumer lets a principal use services that are already enabled; it cannot enable or disable one.
option_breakdown.C: Correct. Service Usage Admin grants the permissions to enable and disable services on the project.
option_breakdown.D: API Keys Admin manages API keys for a project and does not switch services on or off.

questions.title: The value on the Quotas page is a system limit
questions.summary: A system limit is fixed and cannot be raised by a quota request, so the design has to fit inside it.
questions.question: A data team at Marlowe Transit hits a ceiling in one Google Cloud service. On the Quotas & System Limits page the value they reached is listed as a system limit, not as a quota. The team lead asks the cloud engineer to get the value raised for their project before next week's launch. What should the engineer do?

options.A: Request an adjustment for that value from the Quotas & System Limits page
options.B: Turn on the quota adjuster so the value rises as usage grows
options.C: Change the design so the workload stays within the limit
options.D: Upgrade the project's support plan and resubmit the request

explanation.summary: Quotas can be adjusted on request; system limits are fixed constraints of a service that apply to everyone, so the only way forward is a design that respects them.

option_breakdown.A: An adjustment request applies to quotas. A system limit cannot be increased, so there is nothing to approve.
option_breakdown.B: The quota adjuster files increase requests for supported quotas; a fixed system limit is outside what it can change.
option_breakdown.C: Correct. A system limit cannot be increased or decreased, so the workload has to be redesigned to fit.
option_breakdown.D: A support plan changes how quickly Google answers, not whether a fixed limit of the service can move.

explanation.gcloud_command: # Console > IAM & Admin > Quotas & System Limits

questions.title: One more static address is needed within the hour
questions.summary: An allocation quota is freed at once by deleting unused resources that count against it.
questions.question: Brackenridge Media must reserve one more static external IP address in europe-west1 within the hour for a launch. The project has reached its regional quota for static addresses, and a quota increase request may take longer than an hour to be approved. Four addresses reserved for a cancelled campaign are attached to nothing. What should the engineer do?

options.A: Wait for the address quota to reset at the end of the current period
options.B: Release the unused reserved addresses, then reserve the new one
options.C: Retry the reservation with exponential backoff until it succeeds
options.D: Turn on the quota adjuster for the project and retry in a few minutes

explanation.summary: A static-address quota is an allocation quota: it counts resources held, never resets with time, and gains headroom the moment an unused resource is deleted.

option_breakdown.A: Only rate quotas reset with a time period. An allocation quota stays full for as long as the addresses stay reserved.
option_breakdown.B: Correct. Releasing addresses that nothing uses frees allocation quota immediately, with no approval needed.
option_breakdown.C: Backoff suits short rate-limit errors. Here each retry meets the same full allocation and fails the same way.
option_breakdown.D: The adjuster reacts to usage trends over time and files increase requests; it cannot deliver headroom within minutes.

questions.title: A daily API quota that runs out every afternoon
questions.summary: When a per-day rate quota is exhausted long before the day ends, the lasting fix is a quota adjustment, not retries.
questions.question: A translation service at Odessa Books calls one Google Cloud API from a single project. Every working day the project uses up the API's per-day request quota by about 15:00, and every later call is refused until the next day. The API's documentation lists this quota as adjustable. The business needs calls to succeed all day and accepts the higher cost. What should the engineer do?

options.A: Add exponential backoff with jitter to the calls that are refused
options.B: Delete unused resources in the project to free up quota
options.C: Request a higher value for the API's per-day quota
options.D: Send the calls from several service accounts in the project

explanation.summary: A per-day rate quota resets only when the day ends. If normal demand exceeds it, the quota value itself has to change, which is done with a quota adjustment request.

option_breakdown.A: Backoff smooths short bursts. With the day's quota spent, every retry is refused until the reset.
option_breakdown.B: Deleting resources frees allocation quotas. A request-rate quota is not consumed by resources that exist.
option_breakdown.C: Correct. A quota adjustment raises the per-day value so that the calls fit within it.
option_breakdown.D: The quota belongs to the project and is shared by every caller in it, whichever service account sends the request.

explanation.gcloud_command: # Console > IAM & Admin > Quotas & System Limits > select the quota > Edit

questions.title: Stopping BigQuery charges in a retired project
questions.summary: Disabling the API of a storage service does not delete its data, and the stored data keeps being billed.
questions.question: Tolland Insurance has retired an analytics application, but its project must stay because other services run in it. Finance wants every BigQuery charge from the project to stop. The datasets are no longer needed, and nothing in the project should be able to use BigQuery afterwards. What should the engineer do?

options.A: Disable the BigQuery API in the project and leave the datasets in place
options.B: Remove every BigQuery role binding from the project's allow policy
options.C: Delete the datasets first, and then disable the BigQuery API
options.D: Create a budget for BigQuery in the project with a threshold of zero

explanation.summary: For services that store data, such as BigQuery and Cloud Storage, a disabled API leaves the data in place and storage is still billed. The data has to be deleted to end the charge.

option_breakdown.A: Disabling the BigQuery API leaves the datasets where they are, and their storage continues to be charged.
option_breakdown.B: With no bindings nobody can run queries, yet the stored tables are still there and still billed.
option_breakdown.C: Correct. Deleting the data ends the storage charge; disabling the API afterwards stops any further use.
option_breakdown.D: A budget only reports and alerts on spend. It does not stop a service or remove data.

explanation.gcloud_command:
bq rm -r -f -d PROJECT_ID:DATASET
gcloud services disable bigquery.googleapis.com

questions.title: GKE clusters suspended after an API clean-up
questions.summary: Disabling the Kubernetes Engine API suspends a project's clusters; re-enabling the API within 30 days brings them back.
questions.question: Yesterday a script that tidies up unused APIs disabled the Kubernetes Engine API in the project hx-platform at Halix Systems. Today the project's two GKE clusters are shown as suspended and their workloads are unreachable. The clusters and their configuration must come back as they were. What should the engineer do?

options.A: Create two new GKE clusters and redeploy every workload from the manifests
options.B: Enable the Kubernetes Engine API in hx-platform again
options.C: Shut the project down and restore it to reset its services
options.D: Request a higher regional CPU quota so that the nodes can restart

explanation.summary: With the Kubernetes Engine API disabled, clusters are suspended rather than deleted at once; they are deleted only after 30 days, and re-enabling the API reactivates them.

option_breakdown.A: New clusters would not be the old ones as they were, and rebuilding is unnecessary while the suspended clusters can be reactivated.
option_breakdown.B: Correct. Re-enabling the API reactivates the suspended clusters, as long as it happens within 30 days.
option_breakdown.C: A shutdown starts the project's own deletion period and disconnects billing; it does not switch the API back on.
option_breakdown.D: Nothing in the scenario points to quota. The clusters are suspended because their API is disabled.

questions.title: Load tests that starve production of API quota
questions.summary: Quota is counted per project and shared by everything in it, so workloads that must not compete need separate projects.
questions.question: At Sennet Payments, a production service and the QA team's load tests run in the same project and call the same Google Cloud API. During each load test the project's per-minute request quota for the API is used up and production calls are refused. Production must never lose quota to the tests again. What should the engineer do?

options.A: Give the load tests their own service account in the same project
options.B: Move the load tests into a separate project
options.C: Run the load tests from VMs in a different region
options.D: Send the load-test calls from a different range of IP addresses

explanation.summary: Quotas generally apply to a project. Usage in one project does not draw on another project's quota, while inside a project all callers share the same quota.

option_breakdown.A: A second service account still calls from the same project, and the project's quota is shared by all of its callers.
option_breakdown.B: Correct. A separate project has its own quota, so load tests there cannot consume production's.
option_breakdown.C: The request quota is counted for the project; where in the world the calling VMs run does not split it.
option_breakdown.D: A project's quota is shared across all IP addresses, so new source addresses draw on the same pool.

questions.title: gcloud services enable fails in one project only
questions.summary: Enabling a service goes through the Service Usage API, which must itself be enabled in the project making the request.
questions.question: A deployment pipeline at Corbel Energy runs gcloud services enable for several APIs in each project. Its service account has Service Usage Admin on every project, and every project is linked to billing. In the project ce-meter the command fails with an error saying the Service Usage API is disabled; an engineer had switched that API off there last week. What should the engineer do?

options.A: Grant the pipeline's service account the Owner role on ce-meter
options.B: Request a higher quota for Service Usage requests in ce-meter
options.C: Enable the Service Usage API in ce-meter again
options.D: Link ce-meter to a different Cloud Billing account

explanation.summary: The Service Usage API is on by default and is what processes requests to enable other services. If it has been disabled in a project, those requests fail until it is re-enabled.

option_breakdown.A: The account already has the role that enabling services needs; a broader role does not switch a disabled API back on.
option_breakdown.B: The error reports a disabled API, not an exhausted quota, so more quota changes nothing.
option_breakdown.C: Correct. Re-enabling the Service Usage API in the project lets requests to enable other services work again.
option_breakdown.D: The project is already linked to billing, and the billing account has no bearing on whether this API is enabled.

questions.title: Admin Activity logs kept for three years
questions.summary: The _Required bucket's 400-day retention is fixed, so longer retention needs a sink to a bucket whose retention can be set.
questions.question: A new compliance rule at Aldgate Bank says Admin Activity audit logs written by the project ab-core from now on must be kept in Cloud Logging for three years. These logs are stored in the project's _Required log bucket, which retains them for 400 days. What should the engineer set up?

options.A: A retention period of 1,095 days on the _Required log bucket
options.B: A retention period of 1,095 days on the _Default log bucket
options.C: A sink that routes these logs to a user-defined log bucket with 1,095 days of retention
options.D: Data Access audit logs for all services in ab-core

explanation.summary: The _Required bucket's retention cannot be changed. A user-defined log bucket accepts custom retention, and a sink can route a copy of the Admin Activity logs into it.

option_breakdown.A: The _Required bucket keeps entries for 400 days and that period cannot be changed.
option_breakdown.B: Admin Activity logs are stored in _Required, not _Default, so a longer _Default retention does not cover them.
option_breakdown.C: Correct. A sink to a user-defined bucket with three-year retention keeps the entries for the required time.
option_breakdown.D: Data Access logs are a different kind of audit log; enabling them does not lengthen how long Admin Activity logs are kept.

explanation.gcloud_command:
gcloud logging buckets create audit-3y --location=global --retention-days=1095
gcloud logging sinks create admin-activity-3y logging.googleapis.com/projects/ab-core/locations/global/buckets/audit-3y --log-filter='logName:"cloudaudit.googleapis.com%2Factivity"'

questions.title: A log bucket created in the wrong region
questions.summary: A log bucket's region is fixed at creation; moving means a new bucket in the right region and redirecting the sinks.
questions.question: Six months ago Veldt Pharma created the user-defined log bucket app-logs in the global location, and a sink routes application logs into it. A new policy requires that application logs written from now on are stored in europe-west3. What should the engineer do?

options.A: Update the app-logs bucket and change its location to europe-west3
options.B: Set the organization's default Logging storage location to europe-west3
options.C: Add a CMEK key from europe-west3 to the app-logs bucket
options.D: Create a log bucket in europe-west3 and point the sink at it

explanation.summary: The region of a log bucket cannot be changed after creation. The supported path is a new bucket in the target region, with the sinks redirected to it.

option_breakdown.A: A log bucket's region cannot be changed once the bucket exists, so there is no such update.
option_breakdown.B: Default settings decide where the system buckets of new projects are created; they do not move an existing user-defined bucket.
option_breakdown.C: A key's region controls where the key lives; it does not move the log entries out of the global bucket.
option_breakdown.D: Correct. A new bucket in europe-west3 with the sink redirected to it stores new entries in that region.

explanation.gcloud_command:
gcloud logging buckets create app-logs-eu --location=europe-west3
gcloud logging sinks update SINK_NAME logging.googleapis.com/projects/PROJECT_ID/locations/europe-west3/buckets/app-logs-eu

questions.title: Managers who only look at the dashboards
questions.summary: Monitoring Viewer gives read-only access to dashboards and alerting policies without exposing the project's other resources.
questions.question: Tarn Hill Retail runs a dedicated monitoring project. Its department managers must be able to open the custom dashboards and see the alerting policies in that project. They must not be able to change any Monitoring configuration, and they should receive no access to anything in the project outside Cloud Monitoring. Which role should the managers' group be granted on the monitoring project?

options.A: Monitoring Viewer
options.B: Monitoring Editor
options.C: Viewer
options.D: Logs Viewer

explanation.summary: Monitoring Viewer is the read-only Monitoring role: it shows Monitoring data and configuration, such as custom dashboards and alerting policies, and allows no changes.

option_breakdown.A: Correct. Monitoring Viewer lets the managers view dashboards and alerting policies and change nothing.
option_breakdown.B: Monitoring Editor would let the managers create and edit dashboards and alerting policies, which is forbidden.
option_breakdown.C: The basic Viewer role reads every service's resources in the project, which is access outside Cloud Monitoring.
option_breakdown.D: Logs Viewer opens log entries in Cloud Logging; it does not show Monitoring dashboards or alerting policies.

questions.title: Joining logs with sales tables in BigQuery
questions.summary: A log bucket upgraded to analytics can be exposed to BigQuery through a linked dataset, with no second copy of the logs.
questions.question: Analysts at Brightmoor Travel want to join request logs with sales tables in BigQuery, using SQL in BigQuery Studio. The logs are stored in a user-defined log bucket in the project bt-web. Finance insists that the logs are not stored a second time anywhere. Which two steps should the engineer take? (Choose two.)

options.A: Upgrade the log bucket to use analytics
options.B: Create a sink that routes the logs to a BigQuery dataset
options.C: Route the logs to Cloud Storage and define an external table
options.D: Create a linked BigQuery dataset for the log bucket
options.E: Create a log-based metric for the request logs

explanation.summary: An upgraded log bucket can have a linked BigQuery dataset. The linked dataset gives BigQuery read access to the entries in the log bucket, so nothing is ingested or stored twice.

option_breakdown.A: Correct. The bucket has to be upgraded to use analytics before a linked dataset can be created for it.
option_breakdown.B: A BigQuery sink writes the entries into BigQuery tables, which is a second stored copy of the logs.
option_breakdown.C: Routing to Cloud Storage also writes a second copy, this time as objects in a storage bucket.
option_breakdown.D: Correct. The linked dataset makes the bucket's entries queryable from BigQuery Studio without copying them.
option_breakdown.E: A log-based metric counts or measures matching entries for Monitoring; it cannot be joined with tables in SQL.

explanation.gcloud_command:
gcloud logging buckets update BUCKET_ID --location=LOCATION --enable-analytics
gcloud logging links create LINK_ID --bucket=BUCKET_ID --location=LOCATION

questions.title: One team may read only its own service's logs
questions.summary: A log view exposes a subset of a log bucket, and IAM on the view controls who can read that subset.
questions.question: At Pellam Insurance one log bucket in the project pi-ops stores the logs of every microservice. The claims team must be able to read the entries of the claims service in Logs Explorer, and no other entries in that bucket. The logs must stay in the one bucket. What should the engineer do?

options.A: Create a log view on the bucket and grant the team access to that view
options.B: Grant the claims team the Logs Viewer role on the project pi-ops
options.C: Add exclusion filters to the sink so that only claims entries are stored
options.D: Create a log-based metric for the claims service and share its chart

explanation.summary: A log view is a filtered window onto a log bucket. Access is granted per view with IAM, so a team can be limited to the entries its view selects.

option_breakdown.A: Correct. A log view provides access to a subset of the bucket, and IAM on the view limits the team to it.
option_breakdown.B: Logs Viewer on the project lets the team read the entries of every service, not only claims.
option_breakdown.C: Exclusions stop the other services' entries from being stored at all, which takes them away from everyone.
option_breakdown.D: A metric shows counts or values over time; the team needs to read the log entries themselves.

questions.title: The founder cannot create a folder
questions.summary: In a standalone organization the Organization Administrator role does not include creating folders or projects; those need additional roles.
questions.question: A founder signed up for Google Cloud with a personal Google Account and received a standalone organization, with the Organization Owner and Organization Administrator roles. When the founder tries to create a first folder under the organization, the request is denied for lack of permission. What should the founder do?

options.A: Sign up for Cloud Identity and verify a domain for the organization
options.B: Add a second Organization Owner and ask that person to create the folder
options.C: Grant their own account the Folder Creator role on the organization
options.D: Start a new Free Trial to receive a second standalone organization

explanation.summary: Organization Administrator manages policies and grants roles but, by design, cannot create folders or projects. An administrator assigns the additional role, such as Folder Creator, including to themselves.

option_breakdown.A: A standalone organization exists so that no Cloud Identity account or domain is needed; neither would add the missing permission.
option_breakdown.B: Organization Owner manages owners and administrators. A second owner has no more right to create folders than the first.
option_breakdown.C: Correct. The Organization Administrator role lacks folder creation, so the founder assigns the additional role to the account.
option_breakdown.D: Another organization would start with the same two roles and the same missing permission.

questions.title: Nobody can set IAM on the standalone organization
questions.summary: An Organization Owner of a standalone organization can grant Organization Administrator again from the Organization details page.
questions.question: While tidying the allow policy of a standalone organization, its only administrator removed the Organization Administrator role from every principal, including herself. Now nobody can set IAM policies on the organization. She is still listed as an Organization Owner. How should access be restored?

options.A: Run gcloud organizations add-iam-policy-binding to grant herself the role
options.B: Sign up for a new Free Trial and move the projects to its organization
options.C: Restore the organization's previous allow policy from the audit logs
options.D: Grant Organization Administrator from the Organization details page

explanation.summary: The Organization Owner role is managed outside IAM, so it survives a mistake in the allow policy. From the Organization details page an owner can grant Organization Administrator to a principal again.

option_breakdown.A: That command needs permission to set the organization's allow policy, which is exactly what nobody holds any more.
option_breakdown.B: A new organization does not restore control of this one, and moving projects out of it would itself need rights she has lost.
option_breakdown.C: Audit logs record what the policy was, but writing a policy back still requires the permission that is missing.
option_breakdown.D: Correct. An Organization Owner grants the Organization Administrator role from the Organization details page.

explanation.gcloud_command: # Console > Organization details > Organization owners > More actions > Grant Organization Administrator role

questions.title: A federated user as owner of a standalone organization
questions.summary: A workforce pool principal can be an Organization Owner; it is added by its principal identifier and accepts an emailed invitation.
questions.question: A standalone organization has Workforce Identity Federation configured with the company's identity provider. The operations manager signs in through the workforce pool and has no Google Account. The founder wants her to become a second Organization Owner without creating a Google Account for her. What should the founder do?

options.A: Add her as an organization owner by her workforce pool principal identifier
options.B: Grant roles/owner on the organization to the principal set of the whole workforce pool
options.C: Create a consumer Google Account for her, because only Google Accounts can be owners
options.D: Add her to the Organization Administrator role, which makes her an owner after 30 days

explanation.summary: Organization owners can be individuals or principals within a workforce pool. A federated owner is added on the Organization details page by principal identifier, and accepts an invitation sent to an email address.

option_breakdown.A: Correct. A workforce pool principal is added as owner by its identifier and confirms through the emailed invitation.
option_breakdown.B: Organization Owner is managed outside IAM, so an IAM grant does not create an owner, and a principal set would cover every pool user.
option_breakdown.C: Workforce pool principals can be owners, so a Google Account for her is not needed.
option_breakdown.D: Organization Administrator is a separate role; holding it never turns a principal into an owner.

explanation.gcloud_command: # Console > Organization details > Organization Owner > Add organization Owner

questions.title: Removing the founder's personal account as owner
questions.summary: A standalone organization must always keep at least one active Google Account among its owners.
questions.question: A standalone organization has three Organization Owners: the founder's personal Google Account and two users from a workforce identity pool. The founder is leaving, and the company wants to remove the founder's personal account from the owners. What must the company do before it removes that account?

options.A: Wait until 30 days have passed since the two federated owners accepted
options.B: Add another active Google Account as an organization owner
options.C: Grant the two federated owners the Organization Administrator role
options.D: Remove the two federated owners and invite them again afterwards

explanation.summary: Owners may be Google Accounts or workforce pool principals, but every standalone organization must keep at least one active Google Account as owner, so another Google Account has to be added before the founder's is removed.

option_breakdown.A: The 30 days is the time an invited principal has to accept; it is not a waiting period before another owner can be removed.
option_breakdown.B: Correct. With the founder gone no Google Account would be an owner, so another one has to be added first.
option_breakdown.C: Organization Administrator is a separate IAM role; granting it does not satisfy the rule about who the owners are.
option_breakdown.D: Re-inviting the federated owners leaves the same two workforce pool principals and still no Google Account among the owners.

explanation.gcloud_command: # Console > Organization details > Organization Owner > Add organization Owner

questions.title: A second standalone organization for the same person
questions.summary: Only one standalone organization is created per user account, but one user can be invited to own several.
questions.question: A consultant already owns the standalone organization that was created when she signed up for Google Cloud. A client that signed up last month has its own standalone organization and wants her to administer it as an owner, using the Google Account she already has. What should be done?

options.A: A current owner of the client's organization invites her account as an organization owner
options.B: She signs up for Google Cloud again with the same account to get a second organization
options.C: The client's organization is merged into her organization as a folder
options.D: She asks the client to move its projects into her own organization

explanation.summary: Sign-up creates one standalone organization per user account. A user comes to own more than one by being invited as an owner of the others.

option_breakdown.A: Correct. One user can be invited to own and administer several organizations, each through its own invitation.
option_breakdown.B: Only one organization is created per user account, and standalone organizations are not offered to existing accounts.
option_breakdown.C: An organization is the root of its own hierarchy; it cannot be attached under another organization as a folder.
option_breakdown.D: Moving the projects would empty the client's organization instead of giving her ownership of it, which is what the client asked for.

explanation.gcloud_command: # Console > Organization details > Organization Owner > Add organization Owner

questions.title: A project owner cannot enable the Shared VPC host
questions.summary: Enabling a host project needs the Compute Shared VPC Admin role, which is granted on the organization or a folder, not on the project.
questions.question: Wexcombe Group is building its network foundation. An engineer who is Owner of the project wx-net-host tries to enable it as a Shared VPC host project and is denied. The project sits in the folder Platform, and the engineer has no roles on the folder or the organization. What should the Organization Administrator do?

options.A: Grant the engineer Compute Shared VPC Admin on the folder Platform
options.B: Grant the engineer Compute Network Admin on the project wx-net-host
options.C: Grant the engineer Compute Network User on the project wx-net-host
options.D: Grant the engineer Owner on each project that will be attached

explanation.summary: A Shared VPC Admin enables host projects and attaches service projects. That role, compute.xpnAdmin, is held at the organization or folder level, so project ownership alone does not allow it.

option_breakdown.A: Correct. Shared VPC Admins hold the role for the organization or a folder, and it lets them enable host projects.
option_breakdown.B: Network Admin manages networks, subnets and routes inside the project; it does not include enabling Shared VPC.
option_breakdown.C: Network User lets a principal use the shared subnets after sharing exists; it cannot turn a project into a host.
option_breakdown.D: Owning the future service projects gives no right to make wx-net-host a host project.

questions.title: Two environment networks that will be peered
questions.summary: Auto mode VPC networks all use the same predefined ranges and cannot be peered with each other, so a foundation uses custom mode.
questions.question: Ravensworth Tools is planning two VPC networks, one for shared services and one for workloads, which will be connected with VPC Network Peering. Later the workloads network will also connect to an on-premises network that uses part of 10.128.0.0/9. How should the engineer create the two VPC networks?

options.A: As auto mode VPC networks, so that every region gets a subnet in each
options.B: As the default network of two new projects, with the default firewall rules
options.C: As custom mode VPC networks, with subnet ranges planned not to overlap
options.D: As one auto mode network and one legacy network, to avoid equal ranges

explanation.summary: Every auto mode network draws its subnets from 10.128.0.0/9, so two of them overlap and cannot be peered, and they may collide with on-premises ranges. Custom mode gives full control of the ranges.

option_breakdown.A: Two auto mode networks use the same predefined ranges, so they cannot be connected with VPC Network Peering.
option_breakdown.B: A default network is an auto mode network, so the overlap is the same in both projects.
option_breakdown.C: Correct. Custom mode networks get only the subnets and ranges the engineer chooses, so the ranges can be kept apart.
option_breakdown.D: Legacy networks can no longer be created, and the auto mode network would still overlap the on-premises range.

explanation.gcloud_command:
gcloud compute networks create shared-services --subnet-mode=custom
gcloud compute networks subnets create shared-eu --network=shared-services --region=europe-west1 --range=10.10.0.0/20

questions.title: A service project limited to one shared subnet
questions.summary: Granting Network User on selected subnets, not on the host project, restricts a service project team to those subnets.
questions.question: The host project of Ostler Foods has a Shared VPC network with ten subnets. The web team's service project is attached to it. The web team must be able to create VMs only in the subnet web-eu, and must not gain access to the other subnets or to subnets added later. What should the Shared VPC Admin grant the web team?

options.A: Compute Network User on the host project
options.B: Compute Network Admin on the host project
options.C: Compute Instance Admin on the host project
options.D: Compute Network User on the subnet web-eu

explanation.summary: Network User can be granted for the whole host project or for selected subnets. A project-level grant covers every subnet, present and future; a subnet-level grant covers only the named subnets.

option_breakdown.A: On the host project the role allows use of all ten subnets and of any subnet added in future.
option_breakdown.B: Network Admin lets the team change the shared network itself, which is central control they should not have.
option_breakdown.C: Instance Admin on the host project manages VMs in the host project; it does not let the service project use a shared subnet.
option_breakdown.D: Correct. With Network User on web-eu only, the team is restricted to using that one subnet.

explanation.gcloud_command: gcloud compute networks subnets add-iam-policy-binding web-eu --region=europe-west1 --project=HOST_PROJECT_ID --member="group:web-team@example.com" --role="roles/compute.networkUser"

questions.title: Two terminals, two gcloud configurations
questions.summary: CLOUDSDK_ACTIVE_CONFIG_NAME selects a configuration for one terminal without changing the active configuration elsewhere.
questions.question: An engineer at Lowmill Data has two named gcloud configurations, dev and prod, on one laptop. She wants one terminal window to use dev and another to use prod at the same time, for every command typed in each, without one window changing what the other uses. What should she do?

options.A: Set CLOUDSDK_ACTIVE_CONFIG_NAME to a different configuration in each terminal
options.B: Run gcloud config configurations activate with a different configuration in each terminal
options.C: Run gcloud config set project with a different project ID in each terminal
options.D: Run gcloud init in each terminal and choose a different project when asked

explanation.summary: The active configuration is stored once for the installation, so activating one changes every terminal. The environment variable overrides it for the commands in the terminal where it is set.

option_breakdown.A: Correct. The variable changes the active configuration for all commands in that terminal only.
option_breakdown.B: Activation is recorded for the whole installation, so the second window's activation also switches the first.
option_breakdown.C: The property is written into whichever configuration is active, which both windows share.
option_breakdown.D: gcloud init rewrites the shared active configuration; the last run wins in both windows.

questions.title: gcloud works, but the local script finds no credentials
questions.summary: Client libraries use Application Default Credentials, which a local shell gets from gcloud auth application-default login.
questions.question: A developer at Finch Abbey installed the gcloud CLI on a laptop and ran gcloud auth login. gcloud commands work. A Python script on the same laptop that uses the Cloud Storage client library fails, reporting that it cannot find default credentials. The developer wants the script to run locally with the developer's own identity. What should the developer run?

options.A: gcloud config set account
options.B: gcloud auth application-default login
options.C: gcloud auth configure-docker
options.D: gcloud init

explanation.summary: gcloud auth login authorizes the gcloud CLI itself. Client libraries look for Application Default Credentials, a separate local credential file that application-default login creates.

option_breakdown.A: This picks which signed-in account gcloud commands use; it writes no credential file for client libraries.
option_breakdown.B: Correct. It creates the local credentials that Application Default Credentials, and so the client library, will find.
option_breakdown.C: This registers gcloud as a credential helper for container registries and has no effect on client libraries.
option_breakdown.D: gcloud init repeats the CLI sign-in and sets a project; the library still has no default credentials to load.

questions.title: gcloud commands inside an unattended script
questions.summary: A script disables prompts with --quiet and asks for a fixed output format with --format, not the default output.
questions.question: A nightly script at Holloway Print deletes old test VMs with gcloud and then reads the remaining VM names from a gcloud list command. Twice it hung waiting for a confirmation, and after a CLI update its text parsing broke because the default table layout had changed. Which two changes make the script reliable? (Choose two.)

options.A: Parse the default table output with stricter grep and awk patterns
options.B: Run the commands with --verbosity=debug and read the log lines
options.C: Pin the script to the gcloud beta version of each command
options.D: Add the --quiet flag to the commands that ask for confirmation
options.E: Request the list with --format=json and parse that

explanation.summary: Scripts should not meet prompts or depend on default output. --quiet, or the disable_prompts property, accepts default answers, and --format gives output in a format that stays predictable.

option_breakdown.A: The default output of a command may change in a future release, so tighter patterns only break in a new way.
option_breakdown.B: Debug logging adds diagnostic lines; it neither answers a prompt nor fixes the layout of the result.
option_breakdown.C: Beta commands are no more stable in their output, and they still stop to ask for confirmation.
option_breakdown.D: Correct. --quiet disables prompts, so the delete command proceeds with its default answer.
option_breakdown.E: Correct. An explicit --format gives predictable output that does not follow changes to the default table.

explanation.gcloud_command:
gcloud compute instances delete VM_NAME --zone=ZONE --quiet
gcloud compute instances list --format=json

questions.title: A contractor leaves a shared build workstation
questions.summary: gcloud auth revoke invalidates a principal's stored gcloud credentials so the CLI can no longer act for them.
questions.question: A contractor at Tamsin Yard signed in with gcloud auth login on a shared build workstation. Today is the contractor's last day. The team must make sure the gcloud CLI on that workstation can no longer act with the contractor's user account, while other users' sign-ins on the machine stay as they are. What should be run on the workstation?

options.A: gcloud config unset account
options.B: gcloud config configurations delete for the contractor's configuration
options.C: gcloud auth application-default revoke
options.D: gcloud auth revoke for the contractor's account

explanation.summary: Credentials from gcloud auth login stay stored until the session expires or they are revoked. Revoking invalidates them on Google's authorization servers and removes the principal from the configuration.

option_breakdown.A: Unsetting the property only clears which account is selected; the stored credentials remain and can be selected again.
option_breakdown.B: Deleting a configuration removes its properties, not the credentials stored for the account.
option_breakdown.C: This removes the Application Default Credentials file used by client libraries, not the gcloud CLI's own credentials.
option_breakdown.D: Correct. Revoking the account's credentials stops the gcloud CLI from acting on the contractor's behalf.

questions.title: A production project unlinked by accident, twice
questions.summary: Locking the link between a project and its billing account prevents accidental moves and unlinking.
questions.question: Twice this year a billing administrator at Estrel Foods, tidying up the Account management page, removed the production project ef-orders from the company's Cloud Billing account by mistake, and its services stopped. Billing administrators must keep their role and must still link and unlink other projects. What should be done for ef-orders?

options.A: Create a budget for ef-orders with alerts at 50%, 90% and 100%
options.B: Remove the Billing Account User role from every billing administrator
options.C: Lock the link between ef-orders and its Cloud Billing account
options.D: Turn on deletion protection for every VM in ef-orders

explanation.summary: A project's billing link can be locked. A locked link must be unlocked deliberately before the project can be moved to another billing account or unlinked.

option_breakdown.A: Budget alerts report spend against a threshold; they do nothing to stop a project from being unlinked.
option_breakdown.B: The administrators must keep working with other projects, and removing one role from them would not protect this link alone.
option_breakdown.C: Correct. Locking the link prevents the project from being moved or unlinked unintentionally.
option_breakdown.D: Deletion protection guards VMs against being deleted; it has no effect on the project's billing link.

explanation.gcloud_command: # Console > Billing > Account management > project row > Actions

questions.title: Pausing spend by disabling billing
questions.summary: Disabling billing stops a project's services and can remove resources for good, so it is not a way to pause costs.
questions.question: To save money during a two-week shutdown, a manager at Pryce Metals proposes disabling billing on the project pm-lab and enabling it again afterwards. The project holds test databases and disks whose data must be intact when work resumes. What should the cloud engineer do?

options.A: Disable billing on pm-lab now and link the billing account again in two weeks
options.B: Keep billing enabled, and stop or scale down the resources that cost money
options.C: Shut the project down now and restore it within the 30-day recovery period
options.D: Move pm-lab to a new Cloud Billing account that has no payment method

explanation.summary: Disabling billing is not a pause. All services in the project stop, and some resources might be removed and become unrecoverable, so costs are cut by stopping resources while billing stays on.

option_breakdown.A: With billing disabled, services stop and some resources might be removed for good, so the data may not survive the two weeks.
option_breakdown.B: Correct. Stopping or shrinking resources cuts the cost while the project stays billed and its data stays in place.
option_breakdown.C: A shutdown also disconnects billing, and some resources may be deleted before a restore, so the data is again at risk.
option_breakdown.D: An account that cannot pay is not an active billing account, which puts the project in the same state as disabled billing.

questions.title: A subsidiary that must pay its own bills
questions.summary: A separate legal entity paying in its own currency needs its own Cloud Billing account on its own payments profile.
questions.question: Corvane Group pays for all its projects through one Cloud Billing account in US dollars, registered to the US parent company. Its new UK subsidiary is a separate legal entity that must receive and pay its own Google Cloud charges in pounds sterling. The UK projects stay in the same organization. What should be set up?

options.A: A second Cloud Billing account on a payments profile for the UK entity, with the UK projects linked to it
options.B: A UK folder for the projects, with a budget in pounds sterling on that folder
options.C: A label on each UK project, used to filter the cost reports of the existing account
options.D: A BigQuery billing export of the existing account, converted to pounds each month

explanation.summary: A Cloud Billing account works in one currency and is tied to a payments profile, which represents the legal entity that pays. A different entity and currency therefore means another billing account.

option_breakdown.A: Correct. A billing account on the UK entity's own payments profile bills that entity, in its currency, for the linked projects.
option_breakdown.B: A folder and a budget organise and track spend; the charges would still go to the US parent's account in dollars.
option_breakdown.C: Labels split the report of one account into parts, but the parent's account still receives and pays the whole bill.
option_breakdown.D: An export is data for analysis. Converting it changes neither who is charged nor the currency of the charge.

questions.title: The finance lead cannot be added to the payments profile
questions.summary: An Individual payments profile can be managed only by its creator and its type cannot be changed; shared management needs an Organization profile.
questions.question: A founder at Nettlebed Labs set up the company's Cloud Billing account two years ago and chose the Individual type for its Google payments profile. The company now has a finance lead who must manage the payments profile together with the founder, but the profile offers no way to add users. What should the company do?

options.A: Change the type of the existing payments profile from Individual to Organization
options.B: Create an Organization payments profile and use it for the company's billing
options.C: Grant the finance lead the Billing Account Viewer role on the billing account
options.D: Add the finance lead as a second Organization Owner of the company's organization

explanation.summary: The profile type is fixed when the payments profile is created. An Individual profile is managed only by the person who registered it; an Organization profile lets several users manage it.

option_breakdown.A: The profile type cannot be changed after the payments profile has been created.
option_breakdown.B: Correct. An Organization profile lets other users be added, so the finance lead can manage it alongside the founder.
option_breakdown.C: An IAM role on the billing account lets the finance lead see costs; it does not make her a user of the payments profile.
option_breakdown.D: Organization ownership governs the resource hierarchy and has no bearing on who can manage a payments profile.

explanation.gcloud_command: # Google payments center > Settings > Payments profile

questions.title: A reseller keeps each customer's charges apart
questions.summary: Billing subaccounts let a reseller on invoiced billing group each customer's projects and charges separately under one parent account.
questions.question: Hartwell Cloud is a Google Cloud reseller on invoiced billing. It pays Google for all of its customers' usage and charges each customer back. It wants each customer's projects grouped and subtotalled separately on its invoice, with billing access for each customer kept apart from the others. What should Hartwell Cloud use?

options.A: One folder per customer, with a budget on each folder
options.B: One label per customer on every project, and a filtered cost report
options.C: One self-serve Cloud Billing account per customer, each with its own card
options.D: One billing subaccount per customer under its Cloud Billing account

explanation.summary: Subaccounts are made for resellers. Each is a billing account owned by the reseller's invoiced parent account: its projects' charges are subtotalled on the parent's invoice and it has its own IAM policy.

option_breakdown.A: Folders and budgets track spending but do not create separate sections on the invoice or separate billing access.
option_breakdown.B: Labels allow filtering in reports; the invoice is still one undivided total and billing access is still shared.
option_breakdown.C: Separate self-serve accounts would each be charged to their own card, not paid by Hartwell on its invoice.
option_breakdown.D: Correct. A subaccount per customer groups that customer's charges on the invoice and separates access control.

explanation.gcloud_command: # Cloud Billing Account API: billingAccounts.create with the parent billing account

questions.title: Paying by wire transfer against an invoice
questions.summary: Paying by check or wire transfer against a monthly invoice is the invoiced account type, for which a customer must be eligible.
questions.question: The finance policy at Maresfield Steel forbids company credit cards and automatic debits. Google Cloud charges must be paid by wire transfer against a monthly invoice with agreed payment terms. The company currently has a self-serve Cloud Billing account charged to a director's credit card. What should the company do?

options.A: Add a bank account as the backup payment method of the self-serve account
options.B: Apply for invoiced billing, and use an invoiced Cloud Billing account
options.C: Create a billing subaccount and pay its charges by wire transfer
options.D: Set a budget on the self-serve account and pay manually before each month ends

explanation.summary: Self-serve accounts are charged automatically to a card or bank debit. Invoiced accounts are paid by check or wire transfer against an invoice, and a customer must be eligible for them.

option_breakdown.A: A bank account on a self-serve account is an automatic debit, which the policy forbids, and no invoice with terms is issued.
option_breakdown.B: Correct. An invoiced account issues a monthly invoice that is paid by check or wire transfer.
option_breakdown.C: Subaccounts are for resellers and are paid through their parent account; they do not change how the company pays.
option_breakdown.D: A manual payment still goes through the self-serve account's payment methods, and a budget changes nothing about payment.

questions.title: A billing administrator who cannot list the VMs
questions.summary: Roles on a Cloud Billing account are not inherited by the projects linked to it; seeing a project's resources needs a role on the project.
questions.question: The finance lead at Sorrel Outdoor is Billing Account Administrator on the company's Cloud Billing account. To investigate a cost spike she tries to list the Compute Engine VMs in the project so-web, which is linked to that account, and is denied. She only needs to look at the VMs. What should be done?

options.A: Grant her Billing Account Viewer on the billing account as well
options.B: Grant her Billing Account Costs Manager on the billing account
options.C: Link so-web to the billing account again to refresh her access
options.D: Grant her Compute Viewer on the project so-web

explanation.summary: A billing account pays for projects but is not their parent in the IAM hierarchy. Projects inherit nothing from it, so access to resources is granted on the project, folder or organization.

option_breakdown.A: Another billing role is still a role on the billing account, and projects do not inherit from the billing account.
option_breakdown.B: Costs Manager covers budgets and cost data on the billing account, not the resources inside a linked project.
option_breakdown.C: Linking again produces the same link; her billing role would apply to the project no more than before.
option_breakdown.D: Correct. A read-only Compute Engine role on the project lets her list the VMs there.

questions.title: Who pays for usage before the project moved
questions.summary: After a project changes billing account, charges incurred before the move stay with the former account and later charges go to the new one.
questions.question: On 15 May the project rm-analytics at Rowan Mead was moved from the Marketing department's Cloud Billing account to the Data department's account. The Data department objects to paying for the project's usage from 1 to 15 May and asks the engineer to make sure Marketing pays for it. What should the engineer do?

options.A: Move the project back to Marketing's account until the end of May
options.B: Nothing: usage before the move is billed to Marketing's account
options.C: Ask Cloud Billing support to split the May charges between the accounts
options.D: Disable billing on the project and link it to the Data account again

explanation.summary: Changing a project's billing account is not retroactive. Charges already incurred are billed to the former account, even if they have not yet appeared in its transaction history.

option_breakdown.A: Moving back would send the second half of May to Marketing too, which nobody asked for.
option_breakdown.B: Correct. Charges incurred before the move are billed to the former account, here Marketing's, without any action.
option_breakdown.C: There is nothing to split: the accounts are already billed according to the date of the move.
option_breakdown.D: Disabling billing stops the project's services, and the earlier charges would go to Marketing's account regardless.

questions.title: Resources stopped when the Free Trial ran out
questions.summary: When a Free Trial ends, resources stop and a 30-day grace period begins; upgrading to a Paid account in that period can recover them.
questions.question: Ten days ago the 90 days of a student team's Free Trial ran out. Its Free Trial billing account was closed and the VMs and databases in its project stopped. The team wants to continue with the same project and the same resources and is ready to pay for usage. What should the team do?

options.A: Sign up for a new Free Trial with another email address and link the project to it
options.B: Shut the project down and restore it to start the resources again
options.C: Upgrade the billing account to a Paid billing account
options.D: Request a quota increase for the project's stopped resources

explanation.summary: An expired Free Trial account enters a 30-day grace period. Upgrading to a Paid billing account within it may recover the stopped resources and data; after it they are permanently deleted.

option_breakdown.A: The Free Trial is a one-time offer for new customers; a second sign-up is not a way to resume an expired one.
option_breakdown.B: The project was not deleted. Its resources stopped because billing was disabled, which a restore does not change.
option_breakdown.C: Correct. Upgrading within the 30-day grace period re-enables billing and may recover the stopped resources.
option_breakdown.D: The resources stopped for lack of an active billing account, not for lack of quota, and a trial account cannot request quota anyway.

questions.title: A billing account closed after a declined card
questions.summary: A closed Cloud Billing account can be reopened only after its payment problem has been resolved.
questions.question: The only Cloud Billing account of Wynford Crafts was closed after its credit card was declined twice, and the services in its projects stopped. The owner has a new card and wants to go on using the same billing account, with its history. What should the owner do?

options.A: Create new projects and link them to a new Free Trial billing account
options.B: Shut down each project and restore it to restart its services
options.C: Resolve the declined payment, then reopen the billing account
options.D: Request a higher project quota for the closed billing account

explanation.summary: A closed or inactive billing account can be reopened, but only once any Google payments issue or suspension behind it has been resolved.

option_breakdown.A: New projects on a new account would not bring back the existing account, its history or the existing projects.
option_breakdown.B: The projects stopped because their billing account is closed; restoring a project does not reopen the account.
option_breakdown.C: Correct. The payment issue must be resolved first; then the same billing account can be reopened.
