option_breakdown.D: The account is closed for a payment failure. Project quota has nothing to do with its state.

explanation.gcloud_command: # Console > Billing > Payment method, then Billing > Account management > Reopen billing account

questions.title: Retiring one of two billing accounts
questions.summary: To retire a billing account without stopping workloads, link its projects to another active account and then close it.
questions.question: After a merger, Aldous Marine has two active Cloud Billing accounts, A and B. Finance wants account B retired so that everything is paid through A. The projects linked to B run production workloads that must not be interrupted. Which two steps should the billing administrator take? (Choose two.)

options.A: Link each project that is on account B to account A
options.B: Disable billing on each project that is on account B
options.C: Shut down the projects on account B and recreate them under A
options.D: Close account B once no projects are linked to it
options.E: Remove the payment method from account B before anything else

explanation.summary: A project keeps running as long as it is linked to an active billing account. Moving the links to account A changes who pays without stopping anything, and the empty account B can then be closed.

option_breakdown.A: Correct. Linking the projects to a different, active account keeps their services running while A takes over the charges.
option_breakdown.B: Disabling billing stops all the services in those projects, which is the interruption that must be avoided.
option_breakdown.C: Recreating projects means rebuilding production from nothing, with new project IDs and downtime.
option_breakdown.D: Correct. With its projects moved, account B has nothing left to pay for and can be closed.
option_breakdown.E: An account with linked projects and no valid payment method fails to pay, which leads to suspended services.

questions.title: Invoices rejected for a missing purchase order number
questions.summary: An invoiced Cloud Billing account can carry a purchase order number that is printed in the header of its invoices.
questions.question: Pendle Aerospace pays for Google Cloud through an invoiced Cloud Billing account. Its accounts payable system rejects any supplier invoice that does not show the company's purchase order number in the invoice header, and the Google Cloud invoices show none. What should the billing administrator do?

options.A: Add a label with the purchase order number to every project
options.B: Rename the Cloud Billing account so that its name contains the number
options.C: Export the billing data to BigQuery and add the number as a column
options.D: Set the purchase order number on the Cloud Billing account

explanation.summary: For accounts billed by monthly invoice, a purchase order number can be set or changed on the billing account, and it then appears in the header of the invoices.

option_breakdown.A: Labels appear in cost reports and exports for filtering; they are not printed in an invoice header.
option_breakdown.B: The account name is a display name in the console, not the purchase order field of the invoice.
option_breakdown.C: An export is a copy of cost data for analysis; editing it does not change the invoice Google issues.
option_breakdown.D: Correct. The purchase order number set on an invoiced account appears in the header of its invoices.

explanation.gcloud_command: # Console > Billing > Payment settings > Purchase order number

questions.title: Disable billing is refused on a retired project
questions.summary: Billing cannot be disabled on a project that holds an active or pending committed use discount.
questions.question: An engineer at Garrick Paper has deleted every VM in the retired project gp-batch and now tries to disable billing on it. The request is refused. The project's billing link shows no padlock, the engineer is Billing Account Administrator and Owner of the project, and three months ago a one-year committed use discount was purchased in gp-batch. What explains the refusal, and what follows from it?

options.A: The link is locked for the first year, so the engineer must wait before unlinking
options.B: The project has an active commitment, so billing has to stay enabled on it
options.C: The engineer lacks Project Billing Manager, so that role must be granted first
options.D: The project has no resources left, so it must be shut down, not unlinked

explanation.summary: A project with an active or pending committed use discount cannot have its billing disabled. The commitment is billed for its whole term, so the project stays linked.

option_breakdown.A: A lock is something an administrator sets, shown by a padlock, and none is shown; no lock is tied to a project's first year.
option_breakdown.B: Correct. Billing cannot be disabled while the project has an active or pending committed use discount.
option_breakdown.C: As project Owner and Billing Account Administrator the engineer already has the permissions on both sides of the link.
option_breakdown.D: An empty project can be unlinked like any other; the lack of resources is not what blocks the request.

questions.title: Cost visibility across every billing account
questions.summary: A billing role granted on the organization applies to every Cloud Billing account in it, including accounts created later.
questions.question: Thornbury Group has twelve Cloud Billing accounts in its organization, and business units create new ones several times a year. The central finance team must be able to view the costs of all of them, including accounts that do not exist yet, without anyone having to grant access for each new account. What should be granted to the finance group?

options.A: Billing Account Viewer on each of the twelve billing accounts
options.B: Billing Account Viewer on every folder that contains projects
options.C: Billing Account Viewer on the organization
options.D: Viewer on every project linked to a billing account

explanation.summary: Billing accounts belong to the organization. A billing role granted on the organization is also held on each of its billing accounts, so new accounts are covered automatically.

option_breakdown.A: Per-account grants cover today's twelve and must be repeated by hand for each account created later.
option_breakdown.B: Billing accounts are not inside folders, so a grant on a folder does not reach any billing account.
option_breakdown.C: Correct. A billing role on the organization applies to every billing account in it, present and future.
option_breakdown.D: A project role shows the project's resources; it does not open the billing account's cost data.

questions.title: A budget that ignores the promotional credit
questions.summary: A budget tracks cost before discounts and credits when no Savings options are selected.
questions.question: A startup at Ivel Park has a large promotional credit that currently covers all of its Google Cloud usage, so its monthly budget shows almost no spend and never alerts. The founders want the budget to alert on what the usage would cost without the credit, so that they know what to expect when the credit runs out. How should the budget be configured?

options.A: With thresholds on forecasted cost in place of actual cost
options.B: With no Savings options selected, so that credits are not subtracted
options.C: With the amount set to last month's spend in place of a fixed amount
options.D: With a custom time range that ends on the day the credit expires

explanation.summary: By default a budget subtracts all discounts and credits from cost. Clearing the Savings options makes it track the cost of usage before any credit is applied.

option_breakdown.A: A forecast is still calculated on spend after credits, so it stays close to zero while the credit lasts.
option_breakdown.B: Correct. With no Savings selected, the budget tracks spend before discounts and credits are applied.
option_breakdown.C: Last month's spend, with credits applied, was almost nothing, so the target would be almost nothing too.
option_breakdown.D: The time range changes which dates are tracked, not whether the credit is subtracted from the cost.

questions.title: A team lead who manages budgets and nothing else
questions.summary: Billing Account Costs Manager can create and edit budgets without the rights to link projects or administer the billing account.
questions.question: At Hexham Dairy a FinOps analyst must create, change and delete budgets on the company's Cloud Billing account and view its cost reports. The analyst must not be able to link or unlink projects, change payment settings, or manage who has access to the billing account. Which role should the analyst be granted on the billing account?

options.A: Billing Account Administrator
options.B: Billing Account Viewer
options.C: Billing Account User
options.D: Billing Account Costs Manager

explanation.summary: Creating and managing budgets needs Billing Account Costs Manager or Billing Account Administrator. Costs Manager is the narrower of the two, limited to cost data and budgets.

option_breakdown.A: The administrator role can manage budgets, but it also links projects, changes payment settings and manages access.
option_breakdown.B: Billing Account Viewer can read costs and budgets but cannot create or change a budget.
option_breakdown.C: Billing Account User is the role for linking projects to the account, which the analyst must not do.
option_breakdown.D: Correct. Costs Manager can create and manage budgets and view costs, without the administrative rights.

questions.title: A budget for a grant that runs mid-April to June
questions.summary: A budget with a custom time range tracks spend between two chosen dates and does not reset each calendar period.
questions.question: A research project at Calloway Institute has been running, and spending, in its Google Cloud project since January. It is now funded by a grant of 40,000 dollars that must cover all Google Cloud spend from 15 April to 30 June. The principal investigator wants email alerts when 50%, 80% and 100% of the grant has actually been spent over that whole period. Which budget should be created for the project?

options.A: A monthly budget of 40,000 dollars with the three thresholds
options.B: A quarterly budget of 40,000 dollars with the three thresholds
options.C: A yearly budget of 40,000 dollars with the three thresholds
options.D: A custom range budget of 40,000 dollars with the three thresholds

explanation.summary: Calendar budgets reset at the start of each month, quarter or year. A custom range budget is non-recurring and accumulates actual spend between the dates that are set.

option_breakdown.A: A monthly budget returns to zero on 1 May and 1 June, so it never adds up the whole grant period.
option_breakdown.B: The calendar quarter starts on 1 April, so spend from before the grant began would count against it.
option_breakdown.C: A yearly budget counts spend from 1 January and keeps counting after 30 June.
option_breakdown.D: Correct. A custom range budget begins and ends on the grant's dates and tracks the spend across them.

questions.title: Monthly cost trends per service, nothing finer
questions.summary: The standard usage cost export is enough for broad trends by service, project and label; the detailed export adds resource-level rows.
questions.question: The finance team at Orchard Lane wants a BigQuery table of Cloud Billing data to chart monthly cost trends by service, project and label. They will never look at individual resources such as a single VM or disk, and they want to store and query as little data as possible. Which export should be enabled?

options.A: The detailed usage cost export
options.B: The standard usage cost export
options.C: The pricing export
options.D: A Cloud Logging sink to BigQuery

explanation.summary: The standard usage cost export carries services, SKUs, projects, labels, cost and credits, which is what broad trend analysis needs. The detailed export holds all of that plus a row per resource.

option_breakdown.A: The detailed export adds resource-level rows the team will never use, which means more data to store and scan.
option_breakdown.B: Correct. The standard export has cost by service, project and label and is meant for analysing broad trends.
option_breakdown.C: The pricing export lists SKU prices; it contains nothing about what the company used or was charged.
option_breakdown.D: A log sink exports log entries, not Cloud Billing cost data.

explanation.gcloud_command: # Console > Billing > Billing export > BigQuery export > Standard usage cost > Edit settings

questions.title: Last month's costs in a new billing export
questions.summary: A billing export into a multi-region dataset is backfilled for the current and previous month; a regional dataset gets data only from the day of enabling.
questions.question: On 20 March the FinOps team at Dunster Rail enables the detailed usage cost export for the first time. They need the export to also contain the costs of February and of 1 to 19 March. The data must stay in the European Union. Which location should the BigQuery dataset use?

options.A: The EU multi-region
options.B: The region europe-west1
options.C: The region europe-west3
options.D: The US multi-region

explanation.summary: For usage cost exports, a dataset in a multi-region (EU or US) receives data retroactively for the current and previous month. A dataset in a single region receives data only from the date the export was enabled.

option_breakdown.A: Correct. The EU multi-region keeps the data in the EU and is backfilled for the current and the previous month.
option_breakdown.B: A regional dataset gets no retroactive data, so February and early March would be missing.
option_breakdown.C: This is also a single region, so the export would start on 20 March with nothing earlier.
option_breakdown.D: The US multi-region would be backfilled, but it stores the data outside the European Union.

questions.title: When to switch on the billing export
questions.summary: A billing export collects data only from about the time it is enabled, so it must be enabled before the history is needed.
questions.question: Brackley Foods has just created its Cloud Billing account and linked its first projects. Finance says it will not analyse costs in BigQuery until the yearly review in ten months, when it will want a full year of cost data broken down by project and label. When should the engineer enable the Cloud Billing export to BigQuery?

options.A: In ten months, because the export then loads the whole billing history
options.B: After the first invoice, because the export needs one closed invoice
options.C: Now, because the export does not go back further than the previous month
options.D: Never, because Cloud Billing reports can be queried with SQL at any time

explanation.summary: An export does not load an account's history. At best a multi-region dataset is backfilled for the current and previous month; a regional one starts on the day of enabling. Data for the review has to be collected from the start.

option_breakdown.A: Enabling in ten months would yield at most the then-current and previous month, not a year.
option_breakdown.B: The export does not depend on invoices; waiting only loses the usage data of the weeks before it.
option_breakdown.C: Correct. Data is collected from about the time of enabling, so the export has to be on from the beginning.
option_breakdown.D: Cloud Billing reports are charts in the console; they are not a BigQuery table that SQL can query.

explanation.gcloud_command: # Console > Billing > Billing export > BigQuery export > Edit settings

questions.title: Invalid dataset region when saving the export
questions.summary: Cloud Billing export supports the EU and US multi-regions and only some regions; an unsupported dataset region is rejected.
questions.question: An engineer at Selwyn Glass creates a BigQuery dataset in a region close to the office and selects it in the Cloud Billing export settings. Saving the settings fails with the error Invalid dataset region. The engineer is Billing Account Administrator and owns the dataset's project. What should the engineer do?

options.A: Grant the billing account's service agent BigQuery Admin on the dataset
options.B: Enable the BigQuery Data Transfer Service API and save the settings again
options.C: Wait one day for the new dataset to become visible to Cloud Billing
options.D: Use a dataset in a supported location, such as the EU or US multi-region

explanation.summary: The export can write to datasets in the EU or US multi-regions and in a subset of regions. Choosing a dataset in any other region produces the Invalid dataset region error.

option_breakdown.A: The error names the dataset's region, not a missing permission, and the engineer already has the roles needed.
option_breakdown.B: The error is about where the dataset is located; enabling another API does not change its location.
option_breakdown.C: The dataset is visible already, since it could be selected. Its region will be just as unsupported tomorrow.
option_breakdown.D: Correct. The export accepts only supported locations, so the dataset must be in one of them.

questions.title: Stopping a sandbox's charges when its budget runs out
questions.summary: Budgets only notify. To stop charges, publish budget notifications to Pub/Sub and have a function disable billing on the project.
questions.question: Students at Ellery College each get a sandbox project with a $50 budget. When a project's actual spend reaches the budget, all its charges must stop automatically, even if the sandbox is lost. Nobody watches the alert emails. What should you configure?

options.A: Lower Compute Engine CPU and Cloud Storage quotas in each project to match the budget.
options.B: A spending limit on the billing account, applied to each sandbox project separately.
options.C: A budget per project that emails the course administrators at 50%, 90% and 100% of the amount.
options.D: Budget notifications to Pub/Sub, and a function that disables billing on the project at 100%.

explanation.summary: A Cloud Billing budget sends notifications but never caps spend by itself. Programmatic notifications to Pub/Sub can trigger a function that unlinks the project's billing account, which stops billable services, so data in the project may be lost.

option_breakdown.A: Quotas limit some resources but not every billable service, so charges could still exceed $50.
option_breakdown.B: Cloud Billing has no per-project spending limit to set; budgets are the cost-control tool, and they only notify.
option_breakdown.C: Emails only inform people, and the stem says nobody acts on them, so charges continue.
option_breakdown.D: Correct. The function reacts to the budget's Pub/Sub message and disables billing on the project, which stops its charges.

questions.title: No public buckets, but partners still get access
questions.summary: Public access prevention blocks allUsers and allAuthenticatedUsers on every bucket; uniform bucket-level access turns ACLs off; neither blocks named external accounts.
questions.question: Across every project in Brennock Health's organization, no Cloud Storage bucket or object may ever be made public, and object ACLs must not be usable to grant access. Some buckets are shared with named accounts at partner companies' own domains, and that must keep working. Which two organization policy constraints should you enforce? (Choose two.)

options.A: gcp.resourceLocations, limited to EU locations
options.B: storage.uniformBucketLevelAccess
options.C: iam.allowedPolicyMemberDomains, limited to Brennock's customer ID
options.D: iam.disableServiceAccountKeyCreation

explanation.summary: Public access prevention stops any grant to allUsers or allAuthenticatedUsers on buckets and objects. Enforcing uniform bucket-level access disables ACLs, so access is only through IAM. Neither restricts grants to named partner accounts.

option_breakdown.A: Resource locations control where data lives, not who may read it.
option_breakdown.B: Correct. With uniform bucket-level access enforced, ACLs can't grant access to anything.
option_breakdown.C: Domain restricted sharing would block public access too, but it also blocks the partners' accounts from other domains, which must keep working.
option_breakdown.D: Blocking key creation is a credential control; it doesn't stop a bucket being made public.
option_breakdown.E: Correct. It blocks public access on every bucket under the organization, whatever IAM or ACLs say.

explanation.gcloud_command:
gcloud resource-manager org-policies enable-enforce storage.publicAccessPrevention --organization=ORG_ID
gcloud resource-manager org-policies enable-enforce storage.uniformBucketLevelAccess --organization=ORG_ID

questions.title: Autoscaling stopped by a regional CPU quota
questions.summary: A managed instance group that can't add VMs because of a regional quota needs a higher quota in that region, requested through Cloud Quotas.
questions.question: During a sale, Marlow Retail's regional managed instance group in us-central1 stops at 24 VMs although the autoscaler's maximum is 60. The group's errors show that the regional CPUS quota is exceeded. Other regions have spare quota, but the application must stay in us-central1. What should you do?

options.A: Raise the autoscaler's maximum number of instances to 120.
options.B: Request a higher CPUS quota for us-central1 through Cloud Quotas.
options.C: Move the project to a different billing account with a higher credit limit.
options.D: Disable and re-enable the Compute Engine API to reset the quota usage.

explanation.summary: Quotas cap how many resources a project may use in each region. When the autoscaler is blocked by a quota rather than by its own limit, the fix is a quota increase in that region.

option_breakdown.A: The autoscaler isn't the limit; it already wants more VMs than the quota allows.
option_breakdown.B: Correct. A larger regional CPUS quota lets the group grow past 24 VMs in us-central1.
option_breakdown.C: Quotas belong to the project and region, not to the billing account's credit.
option_breakdown.D: Quota usage reflects running resources; re-enabling the API doesn't change it and risks disrupting the service.

explanation.gcloud_command: # Console > IAM & Admin > Quotas & System Limits > CPUs (us-central1) > Edit quota

questions.title: Switching between two projects' gcloud settings
questions.summary: Named gcloud configurations hold a project, account and default region or zone each, and you activate one to switch them all at once.
questions.question: A support engineer at Tavish Telecom manages VMs in project billing-prod in europe-west2 and project lab-sandbox in us-east1, using a different account for each. Twice this month a command ran against the wrong project. The engineer wants to switch the project, account, region and zone together with one command. What should you recommend?

options.A: Install a second copy of the gcloud CLI for the second project.
options.B: Run gcloud init again each time the engineer changes project.
options.C: Create a named gcloud configuration for each project, and activate the one needed.
options.D: Add --project to every command and set the region in an environment variable.

explanation.summary: A gcloud configuration is a named set of properties such as account, project, compute/region and compute/zone. Activating one switches all of them in one step.

option_breakdown.A: A second installation is unnecessary; one gcloud supports many named configurations.
option_breakdown.B: Re-running init each time is slow and error-prone, which is how the mistakes happen.
option_breakdown.C: Correct. One configuration per project holds its account, project, region and zone; activating it switches them together.
option_breakdown.D: Per-command flags are exactly what gets forgotten, and they leave the account unchanged.

explanation.gcloud_command:
gcloud config configurations create billing-prod
gcloud config set project billing-prod
gcloud config set compute/region europe-west2
gcloud config configurations activate lab-sandbox

questions.title: Contractors signing in with their own company's Okta
questions.summary: Workforce Identity Federation lets users from an external identity provider use the console with IAM roles granted to pool principals, without Cloud Identity accounts.
questions.question: Harlow Engineering hires 300 contractors from a partner whose staff sign in with the partner's Okta. The contractors need read access to BigQuery datasets in one project through the console. Harlow must not create Cloud Identity or Workspace accounts for them, and access must end when the partner disables an account. What should you do?

options.A: Create a workforce pool with an Okta provider, and grant BigQuery Data Viewer to the contractors' group in it.
options.B: Create one service account for all the contractors and share a key for it with the partner.
options.C: Create a workload identity pool with an OIDC provider that trusts the partner's Okta tenant.
options.D: Create a Cloud Identity account for each contractor, kept in sync from the partner's Okta directory.

explanation.summary: A workforce identity pool trusts an external identity provider for human users. IAM roles go to pool principals, such as everyone in a mapped group, and a disabled account at the provider can no longer sign in.

option_breakdown.A: Correct. The pool federates the partner's Okta for people, and the principal set grant gives the group read access.
option_breakdown.B: A shared key has no per-person identity and doesn't end when a contractor leaves.
option_breakdown.C: Workload identity pools are for software workloads, not people signing in to the console.
option_breakdown.D: Synced Cloud Identity accounts are exactly what Harlow must not create.

explanation.gcloud_command:
gcloud iam workforce-pools create partner-pool --organization=ORG_ID --location=global
gcloud iam workforce-pools providers create-oidc okta --workforce-pool=partner-pool --location=global \
  --issuer-uri=https://partner.okta.com --client-id=CLIENT_ID --attribute-mapping=google.subject=assertion.sub,google.groups=assertion.groups

questions.title: Cost per team across shared projects
questions.summary: Labels on resources travel into the Cloud Billing export, so costs can be grouped by team in BigQuery even when teams share projects.
questions.question: At Wexcombe Media, four teams share the same three projects, and finance needs a monthly cost total per team for Compute Engine, Cloud Storage and BigQuery, queryable in SQL. Moving teams into separate projects is not an option this year. Which two actions should you take? (Choose two.)

options.A: Add a team tag to each VM's network tags.
options.B: Create a separate billing account for each team.
options.C: Apply a team label to every VM, bucket and dataset.
options.D: Enable the Cloud Billing export to BigQuery and group the cost rows by the team label.
options.E: Create a budget per project with alerts to each team's lead.

explanation.summary: Resource labels are copied into each cost row of the billing export. With the export in BigQuery, finance can sum cost by the team label across the shared projects.

option_breakdown.A: Network tags only select VMs for firewall rules and routes; they never show up in Cloud Billing data.
option_breakdown.B: A project links to one billing account, so separate accounts would mean separate projects, which is ruled out.
option_breakdown.C: Correct. Labels are how costs from shared projects are attributed to teams.
option_breakdown.D: Correct. The BigQuery export carries the labels, so a GROUP BY on the team label gives the totals.
option_breakdown.E: Budgets alert on a project's spend; they don't split one project's cost between teams.

questions.title: Access that follows people as they join and leave
questions.summary: Grant IAM roles to Google groups managed in Cloud Identity, so that joining or leaving the group changes access without editing IAM policies.
questions.question: At Cresswell Bakeries, about ten analysts join or leave the data team each month, and each time someone edits IAM bindings on four projects by hand, often forgetting one. The team's access should change as soon as HR updates the team's membership in Cloud Identity. What should you do?

options.A: Give each analyst a service account key that carries the roles the data team needs.
options.B: Grant each analyst the roles individually, with a script that HR runs once a month.
options.C: Grant the roles to the company's whole Cloud Identity domain on the four projects.
options.D: Grant the roles on the four projects to a Google group for the data team.

explanation.summary: IAM bindings on a group apply to everyone in it. Adding or removing a member changes their access everywhere the group is granted, with no IAM edits.

option_breakdown.A: Keys are long-lived secrets tied to a service account, not to a person.
option_breakdown.B: A monthly script still leaves people with access for weeks after they leave.
option_breakdown.C: Granting the domain gives every employee the access, not just the data team.
option_breakdown.D: Correct. The bindings are set once, and membership changes do the rest.

questions.title: No external IPs except on the bastion
questions.summary: The compute.vmExternalIpAccess list constraint allows external IPs only on the VM instances you list.
questions.question: Security at Ravenhill Water wants no Compute Engine VM anywhere in the organization to have an external IP address, except one bastion VM named bastion-1 in project net-hub. Developers in other projects must be unable to add one, even with Compute Admin. What should you do?

options.A: Create a firewall rule in each VPC that denies all ingress from 0.0.0.0/0.
options.B: Remove Compute Admin from developers and grant Compute Viewer.
options.C: Set the compute.vmExternalIpAccess constraint at the organization to allow only bastion-1.
options.D: Enable Private Google Access on every subnet.

explanation.summary: Organization policies apply whatever IAM roles people hold. The compute.vmExternalIpAccess list constraint permits external IPs only on the instances in its allowed list.

option_breakdown.A: Deny rules block traffic, but VMs could still be given external IPs, which is what's forbidden.
option_breakdown.B: Removing roles stops developers' work on VMs, and service accounts could still create VMs with external IPs.
option_breakdown.C: Correct. The constraint blocks external IPs on every VM except bastion-1, regardless of IAM roles.
option_breakdown.D: Private Google Access lets private VMs reach Google APIs; it doesn't prevent external IPs.

explanation.gcloud_command:
# policy.yaml: constraint compute.vmExternalIpAccess, allowedValues:
#   projects/net-hub/zones/ZONE/instances/bastion-1
gcloud org-policies set-policy policy.yaml

questions.title: Separating production from everything else
questions.summary: Folders group projects so that IAM grants and organization policies set once on a folder apply to all its projects.
questions.question: Ollerton Group has just created its organization and has 40 projects directly under it. Production projects need stricter organization policies and a different set of admin groups than development and test projects, and new projects should pick up the right settings from where they are created. What should you do?

options.A: Create a second organization that holds only the production projects and their admins.
options.B: Create Production and Non-production folders, move the projects in, and set policies there.
options.C: Label every project env=prod or env=dev, and set the policies and roles by label.
options.D: Set each policy and IAM binding directly on every project, according to its environment.

explanation.summary: Organization policies and IAM allow policies are inherited down the hierarchy. Folders let each environment get its own settings once, and a project created in a folder inherits them.

option_breakdown.A: A second organization splits identity, billing and policies and makes shared administration harder.
option_breakdown.B: Correct. Each folder carries its environment's policies and admin groups, and new projects inherit them.
option_breakdown.C: Labels are metadata for filtering and billing; IAM and organization policies aren't set by project label.
option_breakdown.D: Per-project settings work but must be repeated for every new project, which is error-prone.

explanation.gcloud_command:
gcloud resource-manager folders create --display-name=Production --organization=ORG_ID
gcloud beta projects move PROJECT_ID --folder=FOLDER_ID

questions.title: Self-service projects only in one folder and in the EU
questions.summary: Grant Project Creator on the folder, and set the resource locations constraint on the same folder; both are inherited by the projects created there and affect nobody else.
questions.question: The data team may create its own projects, but only inside the folder data-eng, and every resource in those projects must be created in EU locations. Other teams must not be affected. Which two actions should you take? (Choose two.)

options.A: Grant the data team the Project Creator role on the data-eng folder.
options.B: Set the resource locations policy on the data-eng folder to in:eu-locations.
options.C: Create a VPC Service Controls perimeter around the projects in data-eng.
options.D: Set the resource locations policy on the organization to in:eu-locations.
options.E: Grant the data team the Project Creator role on the organization node.

explanation.summary: IAM grants and organization policies are both inherited down the hierarchy. Setting both on the folder scopes them to the data team's projects.

option_breakdown.A: Correct. A folder-level grant lets the team create projects there and nowhere else.
option_breakdown.B: Correct. The constraint applies to every project in the folder, and only there.
option_breakdown.C: A perimeter limits API data movement; it doesn't control where resources are created.
option_breakdown.D: An organization-level constraint would restrict every other team as well.
option_breakdown.E: An organization-level grant lets the team create projects anywhere in the organization.

explanation.gcloud_command:
gcloud resource-manager folders add-iam-policy-binding FOLDER_ID \
  --member=group:data-team@example.com --role=roles/resourcemanager.projectCreator
gcloud resource-manager org-policies allow gcp.resourceLocations in:eu-locations --folder=FOLDER_ID

questions.title: Analysts can read the dataset but cannot query it
questions.summary: Reading a dataset and running a query are separate grants: queries are jobs, and jobs need BigQuery Job User on a project.
questions.question: The analysts group at Lumen Grocers has BigQuery Data Viewer on the dataset sales in the project lg-data, and no other roles. When an analyst runs a query on a table in sales, BigQuery returns an error saying the bigquery.jobs.create permission is missing in lg-data. The group must be able to run queries with the fewest additional permissions. What should be granted to the group?

options.A: BigQuery Data Editor on the dataset sales
options.B: BigQuery Job User on the project lg-data
options.C: BigQuery Data Viewer on the project lg-data
options.D: BigQuery Admin on the project lg-data

explanation.summary: A query runs as a BigQuery job in a project. Data roles let a principal read tables; BigQuery Job User on the project lets the principal create the job.

option_breakdown.A: Data Editor adds the right to change tables in sales, yet it still does not allow creating a query job.
option_breakdown.B: Correct. Job User on lg-data provides the permission to run jobs, including queries, and nothing over the data.
option_breakdown.C: Data Viewer at project level widens reading to every dataset in lg-data and still lacks bigquery.jobs.create.
option_breakdown.D: BigQuery Admin would let the analysts query, but also manage and delete every dataset, far beyond the fewest permissions.

questions.title: A first regional GKE cluster in a fresh project
questions.summary: A new project needs the service's API enabled, and a regional cluster multiplies nodes by its zones, which can exceed a regional CPU quota.
questions.question: A new project at Quillon Freight is linked to a billing account and has only the Compute Engine API enabled. Its CPUS quota in us-east4 is 24. The approved design is a regional GKE Standard cluster in us-east4 with private nodes: three zones, three e2-standard-8 nodes in each, with 8 vCPUs per node. The cluster must be built exactly as designed. Which two actions are needed first? (Choose two.)

options.A: Enable the Kubernetes Engine API in the project
options.B: Request more in-use external IP addresses in us-east4
options.C: Link the project to a second Cloud Billing account
options.D: Create the cluster as zonal with three nodes in one zone
options.E: Request a higher CPUS quota for the project in us-east4

explanation.summary: GKE cannot be used until its API is enabled in the project. A regional cluster runs the per-zone node count in every zone, here nine nodes and 72 vCPUs, three times the regional quota of 24.

option_breakdown.A: Correct. Only the Compute Engine API is enabled, and cluster creation needs the Kubernetes Engine API.
option_breakdown.B: Private nodes have no external IP addresses, so that quota does not limit this cluster.
option_breakdown.C: A project has one billing account and it is already linked; billing is not what blocks the cluster.
option_breakdown.D: Three nodes would fit the quota of 24 vCPUs, but a zonal cluster is not the regional design that was approved.
option_breakdown.E: Correct. Nine nodes of 8 vCPUs need 72 vCPUs in the region, so the quota of 24 has to be raised.

questions.title: A pipeline creating projects in a standalone organization
questions.summary: A service account cannot be an Organization Owner, but an Organization Administrator can grant it Project Creator on the organization.
questions.question: A startup runs on a standalone organization. Its founder is Organization Owner and Organization Administrator. A CI pipeline that authenticates as the service account provisioner must create a new project under the organization for each customer, and should hold no permission beyond that. What should the founder do?

options.A: Invite the service account to become an Organization Owner
options.B: Grant the service account Organization Administrator on the organization
options.C: Let the pipeline sign in with the founder's own Google Account
options.D: Grant the service account Project Creator on the organization

explanation.summary: Creating projects is not part of the owner or administrator roles of a standalone organization. An Organization Administrator grants the additional role, and a service account can receive it like any principal.

option_breakdown.A: Service accounts can't be invited to become organization owners, and ownership would not add project creation anyway.
option_breakdown.B: Organization Administrator sets policies and grants roles; it does not create projects, and it is far more than the pipeline should hold.
option_breakdown.C: Sharing a person's credentials gives the pipeline everything the founder can do and removes any separate audit trail.
option_breakdown.D: Correct. Project Creator on the organization gives the service account exactly the permission to create projects there.

questions.title: Every gcloud command as the deploy account
questions.summary: The auth/impersonate_service_account property makes every gcloud command run with short-lived credentials of a service account.
questions.question: At Carrow Mills engineers hold no roles on the production project; changes are made as the service account deployer. Creating service account keys is blocked by policy. An engineer has Service Account Token Creator on deployer and is signed in to gcloud with her own account. She wants every gcloud command in her prod configuration to run as deployer. What should she do?

options.A: Download a key for deployer and run gcloud auth activate-service-account
options.B: Run gcloud auth login and sign in with the email address of deployer
options.C: Ask for deployer's roles to be granted to her own user account
options.D: Set the property auth/impersonate_service_account to deployer

explanation.summary: With the impersonation property set, gcloud requests short-lived credentials for the service account on every command. No key exists, and the caller needs only permission to impersonate the account.

option_breakdown.A: This needs a service account key, and creating keys is blocked by policy.
option_breakdown.B: gcloud auth login is the browser sign-in for user accounts; a service account has no password to sign in with.
option_breakdown.C: Direct grants would give engineers roles on production, which is what the company's rule forbids.
option_breakdown.D: Correct. The property makes gcloud use short-lived credentials of deployer for every command in the configuration.

questions.title: A first GPU VM on a Free Trial account
questions.summary: A Free Trial billing account cannot add GPUs or request quota; it must be upgraded to a Paid account before GPU quota can be requested.
questions.question: A startup's only Cloud Billing account shows the status Free trial account. A data scientist needs one Compute Engine VM with an NVIDIA T4 GPU in us-central1 for model training. The project's GPU quota in that region is 0. Which two actions are needed before the VM can be created? (Choose two.)

options.A: Upgrade the Cloud Billing account to a Paid account
options.B: Choose an E2 machine type so that no GPU quota is needed
options.C: Request GPU quota for the project in us-central1
options.D: Create the VM as a Spot VM, which is exempt from GPU quota
options.E: Link the project to a second Free Trial billing account

explanation.summary: While a billing account is a Free trial account, GPUs cannot be added to VMs and quota increases cannot be requested. Upgrading unlocks both, and the regional GPU quota of 0 then has to be raised.

option_breakdown.A: Correct. GPUs and quota requests are unavailable on a Free trial account, so the account is upgraded first.
option_breakdown.B: E2 machine types cannot have GPUs attached, so the VM would not meet the requirement at all.
option_breakdown.C: Correct. With a quota of 0 no GPU can be attached, so the regional GPU quota has to be requested.
option_breakdown.D: Spot VMs with GPUs consume GPU quota too; Spot only changes the price and the availability policy.
option_breakdown.E: Another Free Trial account carries the same restrictions on GPUs and quota requests.

# Console > Billing > Overview > Activate

questions.title: Anyone in the company can open a billing account
questions.summary: A new organization grants Billing Account Creator to the whole domain; restricting it means granting the role to chosen principals and removing the domain-wide binding.
questions.question: Six weeks after Lindale Brewing created its Google Cloud organization, an audit finds that three employees have each created a Cloud Billing account with a personal credit card. The organization's allow policy has not been changed since creation. Only the finance group should be able to create billing accounts from now on. What should the Organization Administrator do?

options.A: Grant Billing Account Creator to the finance group and remove it from the domain
options.B: Grant Billing Account Administrator to the finance group on each existing billing account
options.C: Remove the Project Creator role from the domain on the organization
options.D: Create a budget with a zero amount on every billing account the employees created

explanation.summary: When an organization is created, every user in the domain receives Billing Account Creator and Project Creator. Because roles on the organization are inherited by everyone named there, the domain-wide binding must be removed after the role is granted to the intended group.

option_breakdown.A: Correct. Finance receives the role directly, and removing the default domain-wide binding takes it from everyone else.
option_breakdown.B: Administering existing accounts does not stop other employees from creating new ones while the domain still holds the creator role.
option_breakdown.C: Project Creator controls who can create projects; billing accounts are created with a different role.
option_breakdown.D: A budget reports spend and sends alerts. It cannot stop anyone from creating another billing account.

explanation.gcloud_command:
gcloud organizations add-iam-policy-binding ORG_ID --member="group:finance@example.com" --role="roles/billing.creator"
gcloud organizations remove-iam-policy-binding ORG_ID --member="domain:example.com" --role="roles/billing.creator"
